brief_summary: This pilot study will evaluate the feasibility of a supplemental mobility intervention, the Safe Transfers And Mobility Program (STAMP). This program will be implemented in patients admitted to skilled nursing facilities (SNFs) following hospitalization. STAMP will be administered by a mobility aide who will support patients in increasing physical activity through walking and transfers outside of structured rehabilitation. Participants will either receive high-intensity rehabilitation (HIR) or usual care rehabilitation, combined with STAMP. The two main aims are: 1) determine the feasibility, acceptability, and safety of STAMP, and 2) evaluate the feasibility and variability of patient physical function outcome measures. The study will provide preliminary data on program delivery and safety to inform the design of a larger trial aimed at identifying the most effective strategies to optimize functional recovery in SNFs.
primary_outcomes: Usual Gait Speed
title: Supplemental Mobility

brief_summary:
Emergence agitation is a frequent recovery complication in young children following general anesthesia with sevoflurane. It is characterized by confusion, crying, disorientation, and non-purposeful thrashing during early wakefulness, and it occurs especially often following tonsillectomy due to surgical trauma and irritation in the upper airway. The primary aim of this clinical trial is to evaluate whether preoperative administration of nebulized lidocaine reduces the incidence and severity of emergence agitation compared to normal saline in pediatric patients undergoing elective tonsillectomy under sevoflurane anesthesia.

Participants are randomly allocated into two study groups in a 1:1 ratio:

* Group A (Lidocaine Group): Receives preoperative inhalation of 2% preservative-free lidocaine (2-4 mg/kg diluted to 4 mL) administered via a nebulizer.
* Group B (Control Group): Receives preoperative inhalation of an identical volume (4 mL) of 0.9% normal saline placebo via a nebulizer.

Both groups receive a standardized sevoflurane-based general anesthetic. Emergence agitation is evaluated during the first 30 minutes following anesthesia cessation using the Pediatric Anesthesia Emergence Delirium (PAED) scale. Secondary outcomes evaluate postoperative pain severity (FLACC scale), rescue analgesic and sedative requirements, time to extubation, PACU length of stay, and airway-related or systemic complications.
primary_outcomes: Pediatric Anesthesia Emergence Delirium (PAED) Scale Score
title: Effect of Nebulized Lignocaine on Emergence Agitation After Sevoflurane Anesthesia in Pediatric Patients Undergoing Tonsillectomy

\- Can care providers successfully deliver at least 6 rounds of cemiplimab and 3 rounds of Quad Shot radiation to patients?

Patients will:

* Be given cemiplimab every 3 weeks for a total of up to 8 doses
* Be given Quad Shot radiation (four treatments over two days) every 3 weeks for a total of up to 4 rounds
primary_outcomes: Feasibility, as measured by the percentage of subjects receiving at least 6 planned doses of cemiplimab and at least 3 "Quad Shots"

brief_summary:
Many people who are experiencing homelessness are at high risk for HIV, but they often have trouble getting HIV prevention or treatment. Testing may be offered where they are, but starting medication usually requires going to a clinic somewhere else, and many people are not able to make that second trip.

This study tests a program called CONNECT. In CONNECT, a community health worker and a nurse offer HIV services directly at homeless shelters. People can take an HIV self-test on-site. If the test is negative and the person is at risk for HIV, the nurse can start them the same day on a prevention medicine called PrEP. If the test is positive, the nurse can help them start HIV treatment quickly and connect to ongoing care.

The study will compare this on-site program to the usual approach of referring people elsewhere, to see whether it helps more people start HIV prevention or treatment on time.
interventions: CONNECT (status-neutral, nurse-led on-site HIV service delivery)
primary_outcomes: Track A - PrEP initiation
Track B - ART initiation
title: Community-based Outreach and Navigation for Nurse-led Engagement in HIV Care and Treatment

brief_summary: This is a retrospective observational study. Liver metastasis occurs frequently in digestive-system cancers. Identification of the primary tumor source of liver metastasis may pose clinical challenges. Biopsy is an invasive procedure associated with potential sampling errors. This study aims to develop and validate a non-invasive artificial-intelligence model based on contrast-enhanced CT images. The model integrates CT radiomics and deep learning to automatically determine the primary origin of adenocarcinoma liver metastases, including gastric adenocarcinoma, colorectal adenocarcinoma, biliary/gallbladder adenocarcinoma, and pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. The investigators will retrieve historical medical records and de-identified abdominal contrast-enhanced CT images from patients diagnosed at West China Hospital, Sichuan University between January 2015 and August 2026. No new intervention or treatment will be administered to participants in this study.
primary_outcomes: Overall classification accuracy of the combined radiomics-deep learning model for multi-class primary-site prediction of adenocarcinoma liver metastases
title: CT Radiomics and Deep Learning-Based Non-Invasive Model for Tracing Primary Sites of Adenocarcinoma Liver Metastases: Automatic Differentiation of Multiple Primary Digestive Tumors

brief_summary: Climate change can affect the health of pregnant women and their babies, for example through extreme heat and air pollution. Many pregnant women worry about these effects but do not know how to protect themselves. This study tested whether a short education program could help pregnant women understand these risks and learn practical ways to protect their health. Pregnant women attending an antenatal education class took part in one group education session lasting about one hour. The session covered how climate change affects pregnancy and newborn health, helped women think about their own risks, and taught simple protective steps, such as staying safe on very hot days and on days with poor air quality. Women completed questionnaires before the session and again four weeks later. The study looked at changes in their awareness of climate change, their worry about climate change, how risky they felt their pregnancy was, and their fear of childbirth.
primary_outcomes: Change in Climate Change Anxiety
title: Climate Change Education Based on the IMB Model for Pregnant Women

brief_summary:
This study protocol describes a prospective longitudinal observational study designed to evaluate the accuracy of machine learning models in predicting the short-term (24-72 h) risk of reduced participation (training modification or absence due to health complaints, injury, or illness) among elite youth football players (categories U16 to U19).

Full participation in training and matches is a key determinant of athletic development and squad availability in elite youth football. Conventional injury surveillance typically reduces athlete availability to a binary time-loss state and overlooks the continuum on which athletes remain active despite emerging fatigue, minor musculoskeletal complaints, or functional limitations.

In this study, continuous multimodal monitoring integrates external training and match locomotion (Catapult Vector 10 Hz GNSS / 100 Hz IMU), nocturnal autonomic nervous regulation (WHOOP 5.0 wrist-worn photoplethysmography evaluating resting heart rate, heart rate variability RMSSD, and sleep architecture), daily subjective wellness (AMS Hooper Index: sleep quality, stress, fatigue, mood, and muscle soreness), weekly neuromuscular screening (VALD ForceDecks countermovement jumps and NordBord hamstring strength), and anthropometrics with biological maturation offset.

Participation status is adjudicated daily by designated coaching and medical staff. The primary objective is to develop, compare, and internally validate short-term prediction models for the onset transition from full participation to reduced participation, formulated as a single one-step discrete-time hazard read coherently across 24-, 48-, and 72-hour operational horizons. The study aims to evaluate explainable machine learning models (Survival XGBoost, GAMM with SHAP/LIME interpretation) to support training load management and injury risk mitigation within elite academies.
primary_outcomes: Short-Term Incidence of Reduced Participation (24, 48, and 72-Hour Discrete-Time Hazard)
title: Multimodal Machine Learning for Predicting Reduced Participation in Elite Youth Football

brief_summary: Rotator cuff tendinopathy is a common cause of shoulder pain and functional impairment. Exercise-based physiotherapy represents a cornerstone of conservative treatment, while nutraceutical supplementation has been proposed as a potential adjunctive strategy. This prospective, randomized, assessor-blinded study evaluated the effects of adding a nutraceutical formulation containing bioactive collagen peptides, astaxanthin, trans-resveratrol, and vitamin C (Doltendix®) to physiotherapy in patients with rotator cuff tendinopathy without partial- or full-thickness tendon tears. Forty-two participants were randomly allocated in a 1:1 ratio to physiotherapy plus nutraceutical supplementation or physiotherapy alone. Pain, shoulder function, upper-limb disability, and health-related quality of life were assessed over a 120-day follow-up period

The intervention group will receive pulsed low-intensity therapeutic ultrasound applied to the wrist flexor and extensor muscles, while the placebo group will undergo the same procedures with the ultrasound intensity set to zero.

The main outcome will be pain. Additional outcomes will include muscle strength, perceived exertion, function, range of motion, inflammatory and muscle damage markers, and oxidative stress parameters. Pain will also be assessed 24, 48, and 72 hours after the exercise protocol.

The goal of this randomized controlled clinical trial is to learn if a couple-centered cognitive intervention program can improve cognitive health, reduce caregiving burden, and support overall well-being for community-dwelling older adults (aged 60 and above) with mild cognitive impairment and their spouses. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does the couple-based cognitive intervention improve the cognitive function of older adults with mild cognitive impairment?
* Can the intervention reduce the caregiving burden experienced by spouses who care for a partner with cognitive impairment?
* Can the intervention help reduce depressive symptoms, improve quality of life, and strengthen the ability of couples to cope with the disease together?

Researchers will compare two groups of participants: the intervention group receives the couple-based cognitive program in addition to regular community health education, while the control group receives only regular community health education. The study will test whether the intervention leads to better health and well-being outcomes for both the older adults with cognitive impairment and their spouse caregivers.

Participants will:

* Be randomly assigned to either the intervention group or the control group
* If in the intervention group: join an 8-week structured couple intervention with their spouse. The program covers cognitive health knowledge, joint memory and thinking exercises, communication and coping skill practice, and guidance for shared healthy daily habits
* If in the control group: receive standard community health education about cognitive impairment prevention and care
* Complete health and well-being assessments at the start of the study, 3 months after the intervention, and 6 months after the intervention. Assessments include tests of cognitive function, daily living ability, mood, quality of life, how well couples cope with the disease together, and how much burden spouses feel from providing day-to-day care.
interventions: Dyadic Cognitive Intervention Program for Older Couples
Standard Community Health Education on Cognitive Impairment
primary_outcomes: Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) Total Score

brief_summary:
The liver is one of the most common organs where cancer cells spread (metastasize) from other parts of the body, especially from gastrointestinal cancers such as colorectal cancer. While surgical removal of liver tumors has traditionally been the standard treatment, most patients are not candidates for surgery due to tumor location, number of lesions, or underlying liver function. For these individuals, minimally invasive local therapies such as microwave ablation (MWA) provide an alternative approach to eradicate tumor tissue while preserving healthy liver parenchyma.

Microwave ablation delivers localized high-frequency electromagnetic energy through a thin needle antenna placed percutaneously into the liver tumor. The generated heat induces rapid coagulative necrosis, destroying cancer cells within the target area. In this study, real-time ultrasound combined with CT image-fusion navigation is used to precisely position the ablation antenna within each nodule.

The primary purpose of this study is to assess the therapeutic efficacy and safety of ultrasound-guided percutaneous microwave ablation for patients with liver metastases. Participants receive microwave ablation for their target liver tumors and are evaluated with contrast-enhanced CT or MRI at 1 month post-procedure to determine the rate of complete tumor ablation. Patients are then monitored longitudinally at 3, 6, 9, and 12 months to evaluate safety and check for local tumor recurrence.
primary_outcomes: Complete Ablation Rate
title: Therapeutic Efficacy and Safety of Ultrasound-Guided Microwave Ablation for Hepatic Metastatic Nodules

brief_summary:
Crohn's disease is a chronic inflammatory condition that can affect the entire digestive tract. The terminal ileum is the segment most frequently involved, and approximately one-third of patients present with disease limited to the ileum. In such cases, surgical resection to remove all inflammatory lesions may be performed. This procedure prevents recurrence in about 50% of patients within five years of surgery.

The post-operative setting offers a prime opportunity to study the early pathophysiological stages of Crohn's disease and the risk factors for recurrence. While smoking is a well-established risk factor for recurrence, the role of other factors-such as a fistulizing phenotype or a history of small-bowel resection-remains a subject of debate. Meanwhile, the role of the gut microbiota in this process remains largely unclear. Currently, the prevention of post-operative recurrence relies exclusively on smoking cessation and biologic therapies. However, the efficacy of these biologics-particularly anti-TNFα (Tumor Necrosis Factor alpha) agents-is reduced in patients who received prior treatment with these drugs before surgery. Notably, the proportion of such pre-treated patients has risen over the last two decades, reaching 50%. Consequently, there is a need to expand the range of strategies available to prevent post-operative recurrence. A better understanding of host-gut bacteria interactions could help prevent postoperative recurrence. To date, only \*Faecalibacterium prausnitzii\* and Adherent-Invasive \*Escherichia coli\* (AIEC) have been associated with a lower and higher risk of postoperative recurrence, respectively. However, a randomized controlled trial showed that antibiotic treatment aimed at eradicating AIEC was no more effective than a placebo in Crohn's disease. These trial results reinforce the value of a strategy based on identifying anti-inflammatory bacterial species that may play a protective role against postoperative recurrence.

\*Pilosibacter rotomagensis\* is a bacterial species recently isolated from humans by the INSERM U1073 team; it may play a key role in intestinal physiology. This species is distinguished by its high capacity to produce short-chain fatty acids-particularly butyrate-and by anti-inflammatory properties observed in various \*in vitro\* cellular models.

The hypothesis of this project is that carriage of \*Pilosibacter rotomagensis\* could play a protective role against postoperative recurrence in ileal Crohn's disease.

brief_summary:
This is a single-center interventional study aimed at evaluating the feasibility of a multidisciplinary non-pharmacological approach based on acupuncture, telerehabilitation-based physical rehabilitation, and brain health programs to improve health-related quality of life (HRQoL) and psychophysical well-being in patients who have undergone solid organ transplantation (SOT) at least one year earlier, as well as to provide a preliminary estimate of its effects.

Solid organ transplantation (SOT) is currently the most effective treatment, and often the only available option, for end-stage organ failure. Although transplantation can lead to a restitutio ad integrum from a clinical perspective, the quality of life of transplant recipients, regardless of the transplanted organ, frequently remains lower than that of the general population.

This project stems from the clinical, social, and scientific need to provide a concrete response to this challenge through the implementation of functional, reproducible, and economically sustainable rehabilitation pathways aimed at improving HRQoL in solid organ transplant recipients. The proposed approach is based on an innovative multidisciplinary model integrating telerehabilitation, acupuncture, and cognitive stimulation. Such a structured model of care may not only improve patients' quality of life and subjective well-being, but also represent an effective strategy for comprehensive post-transplant management by helping reduce complications, prevent cognitive decline, and promote a more person-centered, sustainable, and humane approach to care.
lead_sponsor: The Mediterranean Institute for Transplantation and Advanced Specialized Therapies

brief_summary:
The study aims to evaluate exercise habits and relevant health outcomes at 6 months and again 12 to 18 months after participation in the COPDEX trial (NCT06551441).

Specifically, we will investigate the extent to which participants maintain regular exercise in the absence of supervision, how long-term exercise behaviour is associated with quality of life and physical capacity, and identify key motivational facilitators and barriers associated with sustained exercise participation

Primary objective is to investigate health-related quality of life in individuals with COPD at 6 months and again 12 to 18 months after participation in the COPDEX trial.

Secondary objectives is to investigate exercise habits, physical activity levels, cardiorespiratory fitness, lung function, functional exercise capacity, and body composition in individuals with COPD 6 months and again 12 to 18 months after participation in the COPDEX trial; to explore differences in long-term outcomes according to original allocation in the COPDEX trial; to identify motivational facilitators and barriers associated with the initiation and maintenance of regular exercise following participation in the COPDEX trial.

At completion of the randomised controlled exercise trial COPDEX (protocol no. H-24021751), which examined the effects of 6 months of high-intensity interval training (HIIT; three sessions per week) compared with usual activity, all participants were encouraged to either continue or initiate regular exercise. All previous participants will be invited to participate in the present follow-up study, irrespective of their original allocation (HIIT group or usual activity group).
primary_outcomes: Health-related quality of life
title: Long-term Effects and Maintenance of Exercise Habits in Individuals With COPD

brief_summary:
Psoriatic arthritis (PsA) is a chronic inflammatory disease that affects the joints and skin in people who have psoriasis (PsO).

The main aim of the study is to know how well zasocitinib (TAK-279) works and how safe it is in participants with active PsA who have not previously received biological medicines. The study will assess whether zasocitnib helps improve symptoms and slows or prevents further joint damage. Participants will have signs of inflammation in their blood and damage in at least two joints of their hands and feet.

Participants will receive either zasocitinib or placebo during the first 24 weeks of the study. After week 24, all participants will receive zasocitinib through week 52. Participants will be in the study for up to 61 weeks.
primary_outcomes: Percentage of Participants Achieving an American College of Rheumatology (ACR) 20 Response at Week 24

brief_summary:
The technical difficulty of transforaminal epidural steroid injection (TFESI) may be influenced by patient-related characteristics, the target spinal level, a history of lumbar surgery, the presence of spinal instrumentation, and degenerative or anatomical changes at the target level. The inability to predict procedural difficulty before the intervention may result in inefficient use of procedure-room time, fluoroscopy, and personnel resources. This prospective study will evaluate the associations between preprocedurally available clinical and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) variables and objective measures of procedural difficulty.

Objectives

Primary Objective

To determine the associations between preprocedural clinical and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) characteristics and standardized TFESI procedural time, and to identify independent predictors of procedural duration.

Secondary Objectives

* To identify preprocedural factors associated with fluoroscopy time.
* To identify factors associated with the number of fluoroscopic images acquired.
* To identify factors associated with dose-area product/kerma-area product (DAP/KAP).
* To identify factors associated with the number of major needle repositioning maneuvers and the need for additional skin puncture.
* To evaluate differences in technical procedural outcomes among the L3-4, L4-5, and L5-S1 target levels.
* If an adequate sample size and number of outcome events are available, to develop an exploratory TFESI Technical Difficulty Score.

Hypotheses

* Higher body mass index (BMI) and greater skin-to-target distance are associated with longer procedural and fluoroscopy times.
* More severe foraminal stenosis, reduced intervertebral disc height, advanced disc degeneration, and spondylolisthesis are associated with greater technical difficulty.
* A history of lumbar spine surgery and instrumentation at the target level are associated with less favorable technical procedural outcomes.
* The target spinal level is independently associated with procedural difficulty after adjustment for other clinical and imaging variables.
primary_outcomes: Standardized TFESI Procedural Time
title: Clinical and MRI Factors Associated With Procedural Difficulty in Lumbar TFESI

Researchers are looking for new ways to treat advanced and recurrent endometrial cancer (EC) and ovarian cancer (OC). Advanced means the cancer has spread to other parts of the body and cannot be removed with surgery. Recurrent means the cancer came back after treatment.

MK-6255 is a trial medicine designed to treat advanced and recurrent EC and OC. This trial is the first time that researchers will give MK-6255 to people.

The goals of this trial are to learn about:

* The safety of MK-6255 and if participants tolerate it. Tolerate means participants will receive the trial medicine unless they need to stop it due to health problems.
* What happens to different dose levels (amounts) of MK-6255 in the body over time.

brief_summary:
ELITE, Evidence-Based Longevity Interventions and Targeted Engagement, was a randomized, open-label, two-active-arm Phase IIa pilot conducted at Sheba Medical Center in Ramat Gan, Israel. The purpose of ELITE was to characterize individual response to multidomain healthy-aging interventions over approximately eight weeks by combining a clinical measure of muscular, immune and cognitive function with frequent digital monitoring between study visits. The primary outcome was change from baseline to Week 8 in the Muscular-Immune-Cognitive Composite (MIC-C). The study hypothesis was that repeated digital measurements could capture the trajectory of individual response over time and relate that trajectory to clinical change measured at Week 8. Prespecified secondary outcomes included safety, study completion and overall protocol adherence.

The protocol-defined intervention was algorithmic polytherapy, integrating a multicomponent pharmacologic and investigational-product regimen with longitudinal digital response monitoring and physician-supervised decision support. In this eight-week pilot, randomized treatment assignments remained fixed. Algorithm-derived response states were generated and reviewed by physicians but did not trigger treatment reassignment.

ELITE enrolled 31 community-dwelling adults aged 50 to 80 years without diabetes and with a body-mass index of at least 25 kg/m2. Participants were randomized 1:1 to one of two active treatment regimens. Arm A received metformin plus semaglutide, and Arm B received metformin plus empagliflozin. Both groups also received the investigational AgeBiotics products AB-01 and AB-02 as common components of the multidomain intervention. Individual study products could be interrupted or discontinued for clinical or safety reasons under physician supervision.

Between clinic visits, participants completed structured assessments through the ANI.AI application, including tongue, left-eye, right-eye, face and wrist imaging, a short micro-survey and a voice recording. Multispectral measurements of the tongue, face and wrist were collected with a dedicated capture device. These repeated digital measurements were integrated with scheduled clinical, functional, laboratory and multi-omic assessments to create a longitudinal view of biological and functional change during treatment.

The ANI.AI platform generated a Composite Response Score (CRS/ADAPT Score) from longitudinal digital biomarker data. The CRS tracked change relative to each participant's baseline and was used within a Bayesian response framework with four prespecified states for physician review: KEEP, AUGMENT, SWITCH and STOPP. The study also included a complementary longitudinal digital health composite to characterize broader multidomain change across repeated digital measurements. These digital measures were prespecified for evaluation in relation to the Week 8 MIC-C clinical outcome.
primary_outcomes: Change From Baseline in Muscular-Immune-Cognitive Composite (MIC-C) Score at Week 8
title: ELITE: Deep Profiling and Algorithmic Polytherapy to Map Individual Response in Healthy Aging

brief_summary:
Rationale: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) has become the standard of care for aortic stenosis across all surgical risk categories, including low-risk, younger patients (≥70 years). As many of these patients are expected to outlive their prosthetic valves, the durability of the valve becomes an increasingly critical factor. Hypoattenuated leaflet thickening (HALT), a finding on post-TAVI computed tomography (CT), occurs in approximately 20% of patients and is associated with bioprosthetic valve dysfunction. Balloon-expandable valves seem more susceptible to HALT with an occurrence rate of 21%, compared to 16% for self-expanding valves.

A recent study identified underexpansion of the transcatheter heart valve prosthesis as a key predictor of HALT at 30 days, which in turn was associated with a sixfold increase in cardiovascular mortality and a threefold increase in all-cause mortality at 1 year. Moreover, data suggest that, in the absence of post-dilatation, more than 95% of balloon-expandable valve implants exhibit some degree of underexpansion. In contrast, routine post-dilatation enhances valve expansion and hemodynamic performance without significantly increasing adverse events. The double-TAP technique-re-inflation of the TAVI delivery balloon after initial valve deployment-achieves a 9-10% increase in valve frame expansion, potentially reducing HALT risk and improving long-term outcomes.

Objective: To determine whether routine double-TAP post-dilatation after balloon-expandable TAVI is safe and can reduce the incidence of HALT.

Study design: Investigator-initiated, multicenter, open-label, randomized trial with 1:1 allocation to routine post-dilatation using double-TAP versus no post-dilatation immediately after balloon expandable valve deployment.

Study population: 422 Patients undergoing balloon-expandable TAVI for native aortic valve stenosis Investigational intervention: TAVI with a balloon-expandable valve followed by double-TAP post-dilatation.

Study design: Investigator-initiated, multicenter, open-label, randomized trial with 1:1 allocation to routine post-dilatation using double-TAP versus no post-dilatation immediately after balloon expandable valve deployment.

Study population: 422 Patients undergoing balloon-expandable TAVI for native aortic valve stenosis

Investigational intervention: TAVI with a balloon-expandable valve followed by double-TAP post-dilatation.
primary_outcomes: Hypoattenuated Leaflet Thickening (HALT)
Co-primary (safety) endpoint
title: SYMmetric Valve fraME Expansion To Reduce hYpoattenuated Leaflet Thickening After Balloon-expandable TAVI: the SYMMETRY Trial

brief_summary:
This study is testing Family Input for Quality and Safety (FIQS), a mobile-based survey tool that allows hospitalized children's families and adolescent patients to report safety concerns in real-time by responding to a text message link on their mobile phone. The main questions it aims to answer are:

1. Does the way families are invited to use the safety reporting survey (text-only invitation versus text plus brief in-person orientation) affect how many families participate and report safety concerns?
2. Does sharing safety reports anonymously versus with patient identifiers (for example, the patient name or room number) affect how often families report concerns and how hospitals respond?
3. What barriers and supports help hospitals successfully use the reports from the survey to make safety improvements without extensive/dedicated research infrastructure?

Researchers will compare different enrollment approaches and anonymous versus identified reporting across multiple children's hospitals to see which methods work best for engagement with the FIQS tool. Participants will:

* Receive automated text message invitations when their child is admitted to participating hospital units
* Be randomly assigned to receive either text-only invitation or an additional brief in-person orientation
* Use a mobile-responsive survey to report safety concerns during their hospital stay through daily text prompts
* Be randomly assigned to have their reports shared either anonymously or with identification to help hospital staff follow up
* Participate during hospitalization while hospitals learn to integrate family safety reports into their quality improvement efforts
conditions: Inpatient Pediatric Engagement and Shared Decision-Making
interventions: Anonymous Safety Reporting with Impact Website
primary_outcomes: Aim 1: Enrollment Opt-Out Rate
Aim 2: Safety Reporting Rate
Aim 3: Workflow Integration Success
title: FIQS Dissemination and Implementation

brief_summary:
Prolonged sedentary behavior and sustained static postures in modern lifestyles induce musculoskeletal stress, restrict thoracic mobility, and impair diaphragmatic excursion, which can alter postural control, increase dyspnea perception, and affect psychological well-being even in healthy adults. Although breathing exercises are accessible, cost-effective, and non-invasive interventions known to improve ventilatory efficiency, autonomic regulation, and core stabilization, their multidimensional impacts in healthy populations remain underexplored. Most existing literature focuses on isolated outcomes or clinical cohorts.

This clinical trial aims to evaluate the comprehensive effects of structured breathing exercises (diaphragmatic breathing and thoracic expansion exercises) in healthy adults. Specifically, the study investigates changes in pain intensity, dyspnea severity, postural alignment, anxiety and depressive symptoms, and body awareness, providing empirical evidence for the role of breathing interventions in preventive physiotherapy and public health.
primary_outcomes: Pain Intensity
Body Awareness
title: The Effect of Diaphragmatic Breathing Exercises on Pain, Dyspnea, Posture, Body Awareness, Anxiety, and Depression in Young Adults

brief_summary: This study will investigate the acute effects of a moderate-intensity Mat Pilates session on blood pressure responses to mental stress in higher education teachers. Participants will complete two experimental sessions: a control session without exercise and a Mat Pilates session. The intensity of the Mat Pilates session will be controlled using the Rating of Perceived Exertion scale, targeting 12-14 points on the Borg scale. The order of the experimental sessions will be randomized. We will assess blood pressure and heart rate at rest and during a mental stress test performed before and 30 minutes after each session. The two sessions will be separated by 48-72 hours.
primary_outcomes: Systolic blood pressure reactivity to mental stress
Post-exercise hypotension
title: Acute Effects of Mat Pilates on Blood Pressure Response to Mental Stress in Higher Education Teachers

brief_summary: An individual can suffer from knee osteoarthritis, which is a degenerative condition, and while standard physical therapy can assist in some way, improved joint mechanics and decreased functional limitations can be achieved through the use of specialized methods, such as the advanced protocols of Neuromuscular Facilitation. Objective of this study is to use Neuromuscular Facilitation, a technique to investigate in terms of its effect in comparison to standard Physical therapy on the levels of pain, the range and range of motion at the joint, and the overall physical disability associated with knee osteoarthritis. An experiment that involved a randomized group of 54 subjects who were aged between 40 and 80 with Grade 2 or 3 knee osteoarthritis was conducted. Recruitment of subjects was done by way of non-probability convenience sampling at United Hospital in Faisalabad. Subjects were randomly placed in 2 groups: PNF-based neuromuscular facilitation group (Group A) received bridging, side decubits, sural triceps, sitting and standing from chair, lateral walk, going up and down stairs, squating and group B received standard Physical therapy which included cryotherapy and isometric Quadriceps strengthening and Isometric Hip adductor strengthening exercise. The outcomes were assessed using Numeric Pain Rating Scale, Goniometry for range of motion, and The Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Osteoarthritis Index.
primary_outcomes: WOMAC index for disability
title: Neuromuscular Facilitation Protocol on Pain, Range and Function in KOA

brief_summary:
This study evaluated the effects of intermittent phentermine treatment on body fat, estimated visceral adiposity, body composition, and tolerability in adults with overweight or obesity.

A total of 600 adults aged 21 to 40 years with a body mass index (BMI) between 27 and 35 kg/m² participated in a single-center, randomized, four-group clinical trial conducted at Hospital Médica Campestre in León, Guanajuato, Mexico.

Participants were assigned to lifestyle modification alone or lifestyle modification combined with phentermine at doses of 15 mg, 30 mg, or 37.5 mg daily. Phentermine was administered intermittently using a schedule of three months of treatment followed by one month without medication during a 14-month observation period.

All participants received nutritional guidance and physical activity recommendations. Body composition was assessed using bioelectrical impedance analysis and three-dimensional body scanning.

The primary outcome was the relative percentage reduction in total body fat from baseline to Month 14. Secondary outcomes included estimated visceral adiposity, waist circumference, lean body mass, body weight, BMI, medication adherence, resting heart rate, blood pressure, treatment-emergent adverse events, and treatment discontinuation.

The study aimed to evaluate the dose-response effects of intermittent phentermine on body composition and the balance between efficacy and tolerability.
primary_outcomes: Relative Percentage Reduction in Total Body Fat from Baseline
title: Intermittent Phentermine for Obesity and Body Composition

brief_summary:
P-EVOLVE is a prospective, multicenter, non-interventional observational study in adults with muscle-invasive urothelial carcinoma who receive perioperative treatment with enfortumab vedotin and pembrolizumab as part of routine clinical care.

The study is designed to describe how peripheral neuropathy develops and changes during treatment and whether symptoms persist at the end of treatment. Peripheral neuropathy will be assessed using patient-reported questionnaires, standardized neurological examinations, and nerve conduction studies. The study will also assess neuropathic pain, neurotoxicity-related quality of life, depressive symptoms, and changes in taste and smell. Objective gustatory function will be evaluated using standardized Taste Strip testing.

Study assessments will be performed before treatment, during the neoadjuvant and adjuvant treatment phases, around radical cystectomy, and at the end of treatment. Participation in the study does not determine whether treatment is started or how treatment is given. All anticancer treatment decisions remain part of routine clinical care.

The study aims to improve understanding of the onset, severity, longitudinal course, and persistence of peripheral neuropathy associated with perioperative enfortumab vedotin and pembrolizumab and to compare patient-reported symptoms with objective neurological and neurophysiological findings.
primary_outcomes: Change From Baseline to End of Treatment in Sensory Peripheral Neuropathy Symptoms Assessed by the EORTC QLQ-CIPN20 Sensory Subscale
title: Peripheral Neuropathy in Patients Receiving Enfortumab Vedotin and Pembrolizumab as Perioperative Systemic Therapy for Urothelial Carcinoma

brief_summary: This randomized controlled study evaluates whether spiritual-based clinical hypnotherapy can reduce anxiety among breastfeeding mothers and whether changes in maternal anxiety are associated with infant weight gain. brief_summary:
Postoperative sore throat (POST) affects 21-65% of patients after endotracheal intubation and is among the most common complaints after general anesthesia. Patients presenting for septoplasty with severe nasal obstruction (NOSE score ≥55) are habitual chronic mouth-breathers, having bypassed nasal air conditioning for months to years preoperatively. This produces a documented state of pharyngeal mucosal dehydration and inflammation that precedes any surgical event - making these patients a distinct high-risk subgroup for POST that has never been identified or studied.

This double-blind RCT will test whether a simple, low-cost multimodal pharyngeal mucosal conditioning strategy - nebulized 0.9% normal saline (5 mL over 15 minutes, 30 minutes before induction) combined with a water-soluble lubricant gel applied to the endotracheal tube - reduces POST incidence and severity compared to standard care (sham nebulization plus plain water on the ETT).

105 adults aged 18-60 years with NOSE score ≥55 scheduled for elective septoplasty under general anesthesia will be randomized 1:1. The primary outcome is POST incidence at 1 hour post-extubation assessed by a blinded PACU nurse. Secondary outcomes include POST severity (VAS 0-10) at 1h, 6h, and 24h; hoarseness; dysphagia; PONV; time to first analgesic; and preoperative pharyngeal mucosal hydration measured by the Modified Schirmer Test.
interventions: Water-Soluble Lubricant Gel on Endotracheal Tube
primary_outcomes: Incidence of Postoperative Sore Throat (POST) at 1 Hour Post-Extubation
title: Pharyngeal Mucosal Conditioning to Prevent Postoperative Sore Throat in Septoplasty Patients With Severe Nasal Obstruction: A Double-Blind RCT

brief_summary:
During resuscitation after a cardiac arrest, providing effective breaths (ventilation) is essential to keep oxygen reaching the vital organs. Research shows that when breaths are given by hand during CPR, they often do not meet the recommended volume, and there is currently no way for ambulance personnel to know this in the moment.

The OXY-VENT study investigates whether a device that gives real-time feedback on ventilation can help ambulance personnel deliver breaths that better meet resuscitation guidelines, compared with using the same type of device without feedback (in recording-only mode).

Adult patients who suffer a cardiac arrest outside the hospital in the Utrecht region and are treated by ambulance personnel will be included in the study. Because these patients are unconscious and cannot give permission beforehand, and treatment must start immediately, the device is already built into the standard resuscitation equipment ambulance teams carry, so no extra steps are needed to take part. When switched on, the device randomly starts in one of two modes: one where it shows the ambulance provider real-time information about the breaths being given, and one where it records the same information without showing it. This determines which of the two study groups a patient is in.

The main question the study aims to answer is whether breaths given during resuscitation more often meet recommended targets when real-time feedback is shown, compared to when it is not. The study will also look at other outcomes, such as return of a heartbeat, survival, and recovery of brain function, although it is not specifically designed to show differences in these outcomes.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of guideline-adherent ventilation pauses per resuscitation attempt
title: The OXY-VENT Study

brief_summary:
Fibromyalgia is a chronic and multifactorial disorder characterized by widespread musculoskeletal pain, heightened pain sensitivity, fatigue, sleep disturbances, cognitive complaints, and affective symptoms such as anxiety and depression. Despite the availability of pharmacological and non-pharmacological interventions, symptom control often remains suboptimal, and currently available treatments may be associated with limited efficacy or poor tolerability. Consequently, there is a growing need for effective, safe, and personalized non-pharmacological therapeutic approaches.

In a previous randomized controlled trial (EXOFIB), we investigated the effects of the Exopulse Mollii Suit, a non-invasive neuromodulation device delivering multisite transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation (TENS), in patients with fibromyalgia.

Using stimulation parameters consisting of a frequency of 20 Hz, a voltage of 20 V, and a pulse width of 55-85 µs, active stimulation was associated with clinically meaningful improvements in pain, fatigue, and quality of life compared with sham stimulation. These findings provided evidence supporting the therapeutic potential of the Exopulse Mollii Suit in the management of fibromyalgia-related symptoms.

However, while EXOFIB established the efficacy of active stimulation relative to sham stimulation, it did not address whether alternative stimulation parameter configurations could yield superior clinical outcomes. To date, no randomized crossover study has directly compared different active stimulation settings of the Exopulse Mollii Suit in patients with fibromyalgia. Consequently, the optimal stimulation parameters for maximizing therapeutic benefit in this population remain unknown.

The present study has therefore been designed to compare the effects of three stimulation modalities delivered by the Exopulse Mollii Suit, including two active stimulation configurations and one sham stimulation condition. The primary objective is to evaluate and compare their effects on functional disability associated with fibromyalgia, assessed using the Fibromyalgia Impact Questionnaire (FIQ).

The inclusion of a sham condition allows assessment of non-specific effects while preserving participant blinding.

The stimulation conditions evaluated in this study are:

* Condition A (active stimulation): frequency 20 Hz, voltage 20 V, pulse width 55-85 µs;
* Condition B (active stimulation): frequency 20 Hz, voltage 20 V, pulse width 100-125 µs;
* Condition C (sham stimulation): brief initial active stimulation followed by discontinuation of stimulation after one minute, while maintaining identical device settings, session duration, and study procedures in order to preserve participant blinding.

By identifying the most effective stimulation setting, this study aims to optimize the clinical use of the Exopulse Mollii Suit in fibromyalgia and to contribute to the development of more individualized neuromodulation strategies. Ultimately, the findings may improve symptom management, reduce functional disability, and enhance quality of life in patients living with fibromyalgia.
lead_sponsor: Institut De La Colonne Vertebrale Et Des Neurosciences
primary_outcomes: Change from baseline in functional disability as assessed using the Fibromyalgia Impact Questionnaire scores
title: Multisite Transcutaneous Electrical Nerve Stimulation in Fibromyalgia: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Sham-Controlled Crossover Trial Comparing Two Stimulation Modalities

brief_summary:
Pediatric strabismus surgery is frequently followed by postoperative nausea and vomiting, which can cause significant discomfort, dehydration, and delayed recovery in young children. The type of general anesthesia administered is an important modifiable factor in preventing these complications. While sevoflurane is commonly used for pediatric anesthesia due to its smooth induction, it is associated with higher rates of postoperative vomiting and emergence agitation. Total intravenous anesthesia (TIVA) using propofol provides antiemetic benefits, and combining it with ketamine may help maintain stable heart rate and blood pressure while reducing emetic episodes.

The primary purpose of this study is to determine whether ketamine-propofol total intravenous anesthesia reduces the incidence of postoperative vomiting compared with sevoflurane-based general anesthesia in children undergoing elective strabismus surgery.

Participants aged 3 to 12 years will be randomly assigned to one of two groups:

* Group KP: Receives total intravenous anesthesia (TIVA) using a combination of ketamine and propofol for both induction and maintenance of anesthesia.
* Group S: Receives inhalational general anesthesia using sevoflurane for both induction and maintenance.

Participants will be monitored closely during the operation and followed for 24 hours postoperatively. The main outcome measured is the occurrence of postoperative vomiting or retching during the first 24 hours. Additional assessments include postoperative pain scores, heart rate and blood pressure stability, the occurrence of the oculocardiac reflex, emergence agitation, and the requirement for rescue antiemetic or pain medications.
primary_outcomes: Incidence of Postoperative Vomiting
title: Effect of Ketamine-Propofol Total Intravenous Anesthesia Versus Sevoflurane-Based Anesthesia on Postoperative Vomiting in Children Undergoing Strabismus Surgery

brief_summary:
Embodiment is an important aspect of virtual reality because it affects how natural and engaging the experience feels and can influence performance and learning in VR-based applications, including rehabilitation \[McAnally \& Wallis, 2022\]. In VR, embodiment refers to the extent to which a person feels that a virtual body (avatar) is their own and under their control. It is typically described as having three components: sense of agency (feeling that one is causing the avatar's actions), body ownership (feeling that the avatar's body is one's own), and self-location (feeling located where the avatar is) \[Kilteni, Groten, \& Slater, 2012\]. While many VR systems aim to increase embodiment, there is limited evidence on which specific techniques are most effective-especially in people with acquired neurological injuries, in whom central nervous system damage may alter body perception and multisensory integration \[Guy, Normand, Jeunet-Kelway, \& Moreau, 2023\].

This study will compare several VR techniques that may enhance embodiment, including synchronized visual and tactile stimulation, heart-rate-based visual biofeedback, increased possibilities to actively control the avatar, and familiarity with the performed action. Participants will include healthy volunteers and individuals with acquired neurological injuries (spinal cord injury or stroke). Across three study days, participants will complete multiple short VR conditions while wearing physiological sensors, and after each VR condition, participants will complete questionnaires about their VR experience. The goal is to identify which VR techniques most effectively increase embodiment and whether embodiment-related responses differ between healthy participants and clinical groups.
primary_outcomes: Virtual Embodiment Questionnaire (VEQ) Subscale Scores (Ownership, Agency, Perceived Change in Body Representation)
title: Investigating Techniques to Enhance the Sense of Embodiment in Immersive Virtual Reality

brief_summary:
Sarcopenia is a condition involving loss of muscle mass and strength that can make walking and other daily activities more difficult. This study will compare a modified seven-form Yijinjing exercise program with resistance training in 240 adults aged 50 years or older with sarcopenia at six hospitals in Beijing. Yijinjing is a traditional Chinese exercise that combines movements, breathing and focused attention.

For the first 6 months, participants will be randomly assigned to Yijinjing or resistance training. Exercise is scheduled at least three times per week, with one supervised group session and two remotely supervised home sessions. Both groups will receive the same dietary counseling and health education. The main question is whether Yijinjing improves physical performance at 6 months by an amount that is not meaningfully worse than resistance training. Physical performance will be measured using the Short Physical Performance Battery, which includes balance, walking and repeated chair stands.

After the 6-month assessment, participants in the resistance training group will switch to standard-duration Yijinjing. Eligible participants originally assigned to Yijinjing will be randomly assigned again to standard-duration or longer-duration Yijinjing for another 6 months. Participants who are not eligible for this second random assignment may continue standard-duration Yijinjing when clinically appropriate. Assessments at baseline, 6 months and 12 months will examine muscle mass and strength, physical function, quality of life and other health measures. Exercise-related adverse events will be monitored throughout the 12-month intervention.

primary_outcomes: Change From Baseline in Short Physical Performance Battery Total Score at 6 Months
title: Yijinjing Exercise for Musculoskeletal Health in Adults With Sarcopenia

brief_summary:
Diminished ovarian reserve (DOR) is defined by reduced follicle counts in women, associated with decreased fertility and lower success rates with In Vitro Fertilization (IVF). Granulocyte Colony Stimulating Factor (G-CSF) is a medication that has been proposed as a potential treatment for DOR, as it may help to improve ovarian function and increase the number of mature eggs available for fertilization. However, the efficacy and safety of G-CSF for DOR in IVF patients have not been definitively established. Therefore, our research protocol aims to assess the effectiveness of G-CSF in improving IVF outcomes in patients with DOR in POSEIDON group 4 (age ≥35 years and AMH \<1.2 ng/mL).

In this double-blinded randomized controlled trial, 140 participants with DOR will receive subcutaneously 5 single doses of 300 μg of G-CSF (Neupogen, study group) or saline solution (placebo, control group), administered as one injection every other day starting in early luteal phase and for a total of 10 days, during standard IVF priming. All participants will undergo ovarian stimulation for IVF in the subsequent menstrual cycle following CHR's clinical protocols.

The primary outcomes will be the total number of eggs and of mature eggs retrieved. Secondary outcomes will include maturation, fertilization, viable day 3 or day 5 high quality embryos and clinical pregnancies, as well as collecting safety data.

Findings of this study may help to clarify the effect of G-CSF on ovarian function and IVF outcomes in women with DOR.
interventions: Subcutaneous injections of a saline solution
primary_outcomes: Number of total and mature eggs retrieved
title: Study of G-CSF for DOR in Patients Undergoing IVF

brief_summary:
The AGREE-BP study aims to evaulate how closely blood pressure measurements taken with an automated upper-arm cuff agree with measurements taken through a small plastic tube placed in an artery, called an arterial catheter, during the start of general anaesthesia.

Blood pressure can change rapidly when patients receive medication to induce general anaesthesia. These changes may be particularly pronounced in patients with heart or blood vessel disease or high blood pressure. An upper-arm cuff measures blood pressure at intervals, whereas an arterial catheter measures it continuously with each heartbeat. Although cuff measurements are widely used, their agreement with arterial catheter measurements during this period of rapid change is not fully evaluated and validated.

This observational study will include 120 patients undergoing surgery under general anaesthesia at University Hospital Graz, Austria. Participants will have conditions that increase their risk of blood pressure changes and will already require an arterial catheter before anaesthesia for medical reasons.

During the first five minutes after administration of the medication used to induce anaesthesia, researchers will record blood pressure using both methods. The cuff will be placed on the arm opposite the arterial catheter and will take measurements at least once per minute, or more frequently if the monitor allows. Anaesthesia and treatment decisions will remain the responsibility of the treating clinician. Participation does not require additional follow-up visits.

The main aim is to assess agreement in mean arterial pressure, which is the average pressure in the arteries over a heartbeat. Researchers will also compare systolic pressure, the pressure when the heart contracts, and diastolic pressure, the pressure when the heart relaxes. They will examine whether patient characteristics or treatments are associated with differences between the two measurement methods and will separately assess agreement during particularly large, rapid blood pressure changes.

The findings may help clinicians understand when cuff measurements differ meaningfully from arterial catheter measurements and inform future decisions about blood pressure monitoring during the start of anaesthesia.
conditions: Blood Pressure Measurement Agreement During Induction of General Anaesthesia
primary_outcomes: Mean arterial pressure measurement Agreement between IBP and NIBP
title: Measurement Agreement Between IBP and NIBP During Induction of Anesthesia in High-risk Patients

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to investigate the correlations between dynamic soft tissue displacement, mechanical properties, and functional recovery across three studies: biceps femoris long head (BFlh) muscle injury, adult acquired flatfoot deformity (AAFD), and medial ulnar collateral ligament anterior bundle (mUCLAB) reconstruction. The main questions it aims to answer are:

1. In athletes with BFlh injury who have returned to sport but remain limited in full participation, does an 8-week Nordic hamstring exercise (NHE) program alter BFlh displacement measured by ultrasound speckle tracking (UST) during maximal eccentric testing and improve eccentric strength?
2. In adults with flexible AAFD/PCFD, does a 6-week intervention of conservative exercise and custom foot orthoses alter the dynamic mechanical behavior (longitudinal displacement and dynamic torsion tracked by UST) and mechanical properties (shear wave elastography, SWE) of the posterior tibial tendon (PTT)?
3. In overhead athletes after mUCLAB reconstruction, does an 8-week blood flow restriction (BFR) training program targeting the forearm flexor-pronator mass reduce regional strain quantified by UST and alter the Young's modulus of the reconstructed graft under dynamic valgus stress?

Researchers will compare biomechanical and functional outcomes within participants before and after each intervention, as well as against comparison groups (athletes with full return-to-sport clearance or asymptomatic flatfoot adults), using UST algorithms and SWE. Depending on their allocated cohort, participants will:

Part 1 (Hamstring Muscle Injury):

* Perform an 8-week progressive Nordic hamstring exercise (NHE) program (for the experimental group)
* Undergo BFlh muscle stiffness assessment using SWE and power Doppler examination for intramuscular scar vascularity
* Complete pain-free maximal isokinetic eccentric knee flexion tests and isometric contractions combined with UST and surface electromyography (sEMG) to measure muscle displacement, scar gap size, and peak torque
* Complete hamstring flexibility testing (active knee extension test) and fill out the Functional Assessment Scale for Acute Hamstring Injuries (FASH)

Part 2 (adult acquired flatfoot deformity):

* Receive 6 weeks of conservative intervention consisting of wearing custom-molded foot orthoses (for at least 85% of days) combined with progressive PTT eccentric training, short-foot exercises, and calf stretches
* Undergo SWE to evaluate proximal and distal PTT shear wave velocity. Perform progressive isometric foot adduction on an isokinetic dynamometer with UST recording raw radiofrequency (RF) data to measure PTT longitudinal displacement and cross-sectional dynamic torsion
* Complete clinical assessments at baseline, 6 weeks, and 12-week follow-up, including single-leg heel-rise tests, isokinetic strength, ankle range of motion, force-plate balance tests, 5-minute walk tests, and self-reported questionnaires (FFI-R, MSK-HQ)

Part 3 (Elbow Ligament Reconstruction Cohort):

* Participate in an 8-week progressive isokinetic strength training program for the forearm flexor-pronator mass combined with blood flow restriction, alongside grip training
* Undergo dynamic elbow valgus stress testing at 5 N·m torque on an isokinetic dynamometer synchronized with UST and SWE to evaluate regional strain and Young's modulus of the reconstructed mUCLAB
* Complete upper-extremity evaluations before and after training, including shoulder-elbow range of motion, isometric muscle strength using hand-held dynamometry, countermovement push-up (CMPU) power tests on force plates, and the Disabilities of the Arm, Shoulder, and Hand (DASH) questionnaire
interventions: Custom Foot Orthoses and Exercise Therapy
primary_outcomes: Longitudinal Muscle Displacement of the Biceps Femoris Long Head (Arm 1)
Posterior Tibial Tendon Dynamic Torsion, Tendon Displacement, and Shear Wave Velocity (Arm 2)
Regional Strain of the Reconstructed mUCLAB Graft (Arm 3)
title: Correlation Between Soft Tissue Displacement and Functional Performance in Orthopedic Patients

brief_summary:
Prostate cancer is the most common cancer affecting men in the UK and is the most common cancer in UK prisons.

Early diagnosis is vital because treatment is more effective when the disease is detected at an early stage. However, people in prison face significant barriers to healthcare, and little is known about how prostate cancer affects this population. This is concerning, as the prison population is ageing, and men over 50 are at the highest risk of developing prostate cancer.

Research shows that prisoners are more likely to be diagnosed with any cancer at a late stage, often through emergency hospital visits, and are less likely to receive timely or curative treatment compared to the general population. Survival rates are also worse. However, there are very little data from the UK describing prostate cancer diagnosis and outcomes in the UK from the prison population, which is why we want to find out information about prostate cancer diagnosis in prisons compared to in the general population.

This project, a collaboration between Oxleas NHS Trust and The Royal Marsden, will test and develop processes for extracting pseudo-anonymised data from the prison population. Using pseudo-anonymous data from prisoner health records in Oxleas NHS Trust, we will assess prevalence and examine how prostate cancer is diagnosed, the treatments offered, and the survival outcomes. We will compare these results against UK Genetic Prostate Cancer Study (UKGPCS) data about men of a similar age in the general population. Our aim is to understand whether prisoners face delays in diagnosis and worse outcomes, and to assess whether prison-based screening could help.

The findings will inform future healthcare research and the development of policies and may support the development of tailored educational resources and screening approaches, ultimately helping to reduce health inequalities and improve outcomes for people in prison.
primary_outcomes: Prevalence, method of diagnosis, stage at diagnosis, outcomes of prostate cancer in the Oxleas NHS prison population
title: Prostate Cancer in UK Prisons: A Retrospective Data Analysis

Outcome measures included trunk muscle strength assessed using a handheld dynamometer (MicroFET3), core muscle activation assessed using surface electromyography (sEMG), and static and dynamic balance assessed using the TYMO balance platform and the Y-Balance Test, respectively.

brief_summary: Domestic Violence (DV) is a major public health problem in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) including Nepal, where women often live in extended, multigenerational households, and violence can be perpetrated by the husband and/or mother-in-law (MIL). DV is a well-established social driver of mental illness and doubles the rate of depression and Post Traumatic Stress Disorders (PTSD). Interventions like cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) can improve depression among women after they exit abusive relationships with DV. However, despite ongoing violence, many young women in LMICs including Nepal are less likely to divorce or separate from their husband. But, ongoing DV severely limits mental health recovery and increases the risks of suicide. This created a need for intervention which improves mental health and reduce ongoing DV, while involving the woman along with her husband and MIL. The study team thus developed a multi-component family intervention and conducted a study to to assess the acceptability, feasibility, and preliminary efficacy of the intervention to reduce domestic violence and consequent depression among married women in Nepal.

brief_summary:
What is this study about? This study will test a program called "Newenkantun" (which refers to a hand-strength game in Mapuche culture) designed to help young children develop important social and emotional skills through play and physical activity. The program focuses on helping children learn how to understand and manage their emotions, get along with others, and make good decisions - skills that are important for success in school and life.

Why is this study being done? The early years of childhood are a critical time for developing social, emotional, and physical skills. Many children, especially those from low-income families, face challenges that make it harder to develop these skills. This study will test whether a program that combines active play, social-emotional learning, and family involvement can help young children in the Araucanía region of Chile develop these important abilities.

The program also aims to help children be more physically active, spend less time on screens, and get better sleep - all of which are important for healthy development.

Who can participate? Children ages 4-6 years old (attending transition levels 1 and 2 in early childhood education) in the cities of Temuco and Padre Las Casas in the Araucanía region of Chile. Both their teachers and parents/guardians will also participate in the program.

What will participants do? Children will participate in play-based activities at their schools over 16 weeks. These activities use storytelling and imaginative play (like pretending to be different characters) to help them practice social and emotional skills. The activities respect and incorporate the cultural background of the Araucanía region, including Mapuche cultural elements.

Teachers will receive training and support (both in-person and online) to learn how to teach social-emotional skills and promote healthy movement behaviors in their classrooms. They will receive materials and kits to help them run play activities.

Parents and guardians will receive support through an online platform, app, social media, and printed materials. They will learn about the importance of social-emotional development and healthy movement habits, and get practical tips for supporting these at home. The program includes 8 topics delivered over 4 months, with each topic taking about 30 minutes to complete.

What will be measured?

Researchers will measure:

Children's social and emotional skills (like managing emotions, getting along with others, and making responsible decisions) Physical activity levels, screen time, and sleep patterns Motor skills and thinking abilities Teachers' confidence and practices in teaching social-emotional skills Parents' support practices at home The school environment and how well it supports these skills

These measurements will happen at the beginning of the program, at the end, and at follow-up visits 3, 6, and 12 months after the program ends.

How is the study designed? The study uses a "stepped-wedge" design, which means that 10 schools will start the program at different times, chosen randomly. This design allows all schools to eventually receive the program while still allowing researchers to compare results. Each school will participate for 16 weeks, and researchers will follow what happens afterwards to see if the benefits last over time.

What are the potential benefits? If successful, this program could provide a practical, culturally appropriate way to help young children develop important social, emotional, and physical skills during a critical time in their development. The program is designed to be sustainable and could potentially be used in other schools and communities in the future.
primary_outcomes: Change from baseline in children's socioemotional competencies as measured by the Children's Emotional Adjustment Scale - Preschool Version (CEAS-P) total score

brief_summary: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is characterized by stomach pain and altered bowel habits. It affects about 5 million people in Canada. Doctors don't fully understand what causes IBS, so treatments often don't work well. Many patients say certain foods make their symptoms worse. This may be due to how gut bacteria break down food. Some bacteria produce harmful chemicals like histamine and lysophosphatidylcholine (LPC)/lysophosphatidic acid (LPA), which can cause pain and gut problems. These chemicals may affect about 35% of IBS patients. The goal is to find out which patients have these bacteria. Then, doctors can give them treatments that match their gut bacteria. This could help reduce symptoms and improve their lives. If the study is successful, it could change how we understand, diagnose, and treat IBS, leading to new treatments that focus on personalized microbiota-directed treatments targeting specific causative mechanisms.

brief_summary:
Benign prostatic hyperplasia is a noncancerous enlargement of the prostate that can cause difficulty urinating. Holmium laser enucleation of the prostate (HoLEP) uses a laser to remove prostate tissue blocking urine flow. Some patients experience stress urinary incontinence after surgery, meaning urine leakage during activities such as coughing, sneezing, or physical exertion. This may be related to temporary dysfunction or injury of the muscle that controls urine release.

This single-center, prospective randomized study compares three HoLEP techniques in men aged 50-85 years with benign prostatic hyperplasia: conventional HoLEP without apical pre-disconnection; HoLEP with apical pre-disconnection at a fixed 12 o'clock location; and HoLEP with MRI-guided individualized apical pre-disconnection. Apical pre-disconnection involves separating the urethral lining near the tip of the prostate before the main tissue removal step. In the individualized group, preoperative magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is used to tailor the separation site to each patient's anatomy.

The study tests the hypothesis that MRI-guided individualized apical pre-disconnection reduces postoperative stress urinary incontinence and improves early urinary control and quality of life compared with the other two techniques, while maintaining the improvement in urination achieved by HoLEP.

Participants are randomly assigned to one of the three surgical groups and assessed at 1 week, 1 month, and 3 months after surgery. The primary outcome is the International Consultation on Incontinence Questionnaire-Urinary Incontinence Short Form (ICIQ-UI-SF) total score at 3 months. This questionnaire measures the frequency and amount of urine leakage and its impact on daily life. Secondary outcomes include ICIQ-UI-SF scores at 1 week and 1 month, and quality of life, urinary symptoms, maximum urine flow rate, and postvoid residual urine volume at all three follow-up visits. Postoperative complications are also recorded and compared among groups.

HoLEP With MRI-Guided Individualized Apical Pre-disconnection

brief_summary:
Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder (OCD) is a common long-lasting, and disabling condition, affecting 1 in every 25 people in Portugal. People with OCD experience unwanted, repeated thoughts (obsessions) and repetitive behaviors (compulsions) that impair their daily lives and well-being. Even though OCD is common, many people do not get the specialized help they need. On average, it takes about 10 years from when symptoms first appear until someone receives proper treatment. This happens mainly because specialized care is mostly available in central hospitals, which makes it harder for people living outside big cities to get help. This delay is caused by a mix of factors: distance from specialized centers, financial barriers, and the stigma that still surrounds mental illness. These are well-known problems, and they highlight the urgent need for treatment options that are easier to access and can reach more people.

The "Being with OCD" study aims to test whether an online program - combining cognitive-behavioral therapy (a well-established talk therapy approach) with mindfulness techniques - can effectively help people with OCD. Digital tools like websites and phone apps have become a promising way to make mental health care more available, more affordable, and easier to reach for more patients.

Recent research shows that online cognitive-behavioral therapy programs for OCD can meaningfully reduce symptoms, working about as well as in-person therapy - especially when patients get some support from a clinician along the way. That said, these digital tools have not been tested enough in real-world, everyday settings, and few have been developed by actually listening to what patients and healthcare professionals need. This is a problem because it leads to low engagement by patients in these programs. In fact, a common pattern has been observed: people tend to start using digital therapy programs enthusiastically, but usage drops off quickly after the first few weeks - largely because these programs are not designed around what users actually want and need.

At the same time, mindfulness - the practice of paying attention to the present moment without judgment - has become an increasingly valuable tool to cognitive-behavioral therapy for OCD. This combined approach can help reduce excessive worrying/overthinking, increase acceptance of difficult thoughts, and improve emotional control, helping people relate to their intrusive thoughts in a calmer, less reactive way. Among the different types of therapy available, mindfulness-based approaches tend to work particularly well in digital formats, with people sticking with them more and reporting higher satisfaction. For this reason, beyond testing whether our program works, this study will also look at how practical and well-received the program is for users.

We will recruit 128 patients with OCD, split into two groups: a control group, who will continue receiving their usual care, and an intervention group, who will receive the online program in addition to their usual care. The program will be delivered through a website/app (usable on a computer or smartphone) and will run for 9 weeks, offering audio recordings, educational materials, and practical exercises based on cognitive-behavioral therapy and mindfulness. The goal is to help patients change unhelpful thought patterns and behaviors linked to their condition. Throughout the 9 weeks, participants will complete some tests and interviews so the research team can track changes in symptom severity, well-being, day-to-day functioning, and how practical and acceptable the program is to use.

If this online program proves effective and usable, it could help expand access to OCD treatment for people who currently struggle to find care.

Testing whether this kind of program is practical, well-received, and effective is an important step toward developing new mental health care options that are both clinically effective and genuinely accessible.
lead_sponsor: Unidade Local de Saúde de Coimbra, EPE
primary_outcomes: Change in severity of obsessive-compulsive symptoms (Y-BOCS-II)
title: A Digital Mindfulness-Based Program for OCD

brief_summary: The aim of this study is to evaluate differences in energy, macro- and micronutrient intakes, dietary characteristics, quality of life, and biochemical parameters between individuals with and without premature ventricular complexes. The study will include a total of 100 adults who present to the Cardiology Outpatient Clinic of Buca Seyfi Demirsoy Training and Research Hospital, comprising 50 individuals with premature ventricular complexes and 50 healthy individuals. Participants will be instructed to discontinue caffeine-containing beverages, stimulants, and medications that may affect cardiac rhythm for 72 hours prior to Holter monitoring. The diagnosis of premature ventricular complexes will be established by a specialist cardiologist. Dietary intake will be assessed using three non-consecutive 24-hour dietary recalls, including two weekdays and one weekend day. Dietary intake data will be collected by the researcher through face-to-face interviews and recorded on the study questionnaire. The Dietary Inflammatory Index (DII) and Healthy Eating Index will be calculated based on the participants' three-day dietary intake data. No additional blood samples or biochemical tests will be requested specifically for the purposes of this study. Instead, the participants' most recent biochemical parameters obtained as part of routine clinical care will be retrieved from their medical records. These parameters will include fasting blood glucose (mg/dL), glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c, %), total cholesterol (mg/dL), high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C, mg/dL), low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C, mg/dL), triglycerides (mg/dL), vitamin D, and other routinely assessed biochemical parameters. The results will be interpreted according to the reference ranges used by Buca Seyfi Demirsoy Training and Research Hospital. Participants' quality of life will be assessed using the 36-Item Short Form Health Survey (SF-36).
primary_outcomes: Diet Inflammatory Index
title: Premature Ventricular Complex and Diet Inflamatuar Index

brief_summary: In low- and middle-income countries, particularly the Lao People's Democratic Republic, limited infrastructure and constrained educational access create competency gaps and limited training opportunities for emergency nurses. As existing evidence primarily involves high-resource settings, its applicability to low-resource settings is limited. Therefore, an Official Development Assistance-derived, culturally tailored emergency nursing training program was developed for the Lao People's Democratic Republic, and its effectiveness will be evaluated. This quasi-experimental study will used a single-group pre-test-post-test design, with data collected using practical performance assessments and self-administered surveys. The six-session program (three lectures and three activities) will be preceded by pre-learning videos and handouts to standardize baseline knowledge. Guided by Kirkpatrick's model, the outcomes include program satisfaction (Level 1: Reaction), cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) and triage knowledge (Level 2: Learning), CPR core skills, triage skills, and emergency nurses' professional competency (Level 3: Behavior). Continuous data will be analyzed using the paired t-test or Wilcoxon signed-rank test, depending on normality.

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to study whether major surgery is linked to changes in the brain that are typical of Alzheimer's disease.

The study is a prospective observational study that will be carried out in Uppsala University Hospital. Adults aged 55-75 years who are healthy otherwise (ASA1) having a hip or knee replacement under spinal anesthesia, and a comparison group of people of the same age and sex with hip or knee arthrosis who are not having surgery will be included.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does the amount of the protein tau in the brain increase in the two years after surgery?
* Are changes in tau linked to inflammation in the blood and spinal fluid, and to changes in memory and thinking?

Participants will:

* Have brain scans (PET and MRI) before surgery and 12 and 24 months later
* Give small samples of spinal fluid and blood
* Complete memory and thinking tests at the same time points

Researchers will compare the surgery group with the non-surgery group to see whether surgery is associated with more tau in the brain and with changes in memory and thinking.
