brief_summary: The first hours-to-day following acute traumatic cervical SCI represent a critical period of time to optimize hemodynamic management. After a spinal cord injury, cardiovascular function is affected. Maintaining blood pressure becomes is an important part of treatment as it supports recovery of the injured spinal cord. Blood pressure is most often increased using vasopressors, such as norepinephrine. Although these drugs help maintain blood flow, they may also lead to increased bleeding in the injury site, making the lesion worse. Alternatively, dobutamine, a medication that helps the heart pump more effectively, has shown to maintain blood pressure and improve prefusion at the injury site. This study will assess dobutamine capacity to maintain blood pressure acutely post injury.

The goal of this study is to find out how safe this special kind of radiation technique is for women with endometrial cancer, both right after the treatment and later on. We also want to see how well this treatment works in stopping the cancer from coming back and how it affects the patients' overall health and quality of life. The main question it aims to answer is:

For perianal fistulizing Crohn's disease (PFCD), combined treatment with surgical intervention (e.g., seton placement) and medical therapy centered on anti-TNF agents is standard. brief_summary: Percutaneous Coronary Intervention (PCI) is a common procedure used to restore coronary blood flow in patients with coronary artery disease. Post-PCI patients may experience reduced exercise tolerance, altered breathing patterns, and autonomic imbalance, which may affect oxygen saturation and heart-rate variability (HRV). Breathing exercises are simple, non-pharmacological interventions that may support early recovery. This randomized controlled trial aims to compare the effects of Pilates breathing and diaphragmatic breathing on oxygen saturation and HRV in hemodynamically stable post-PCI patients. A total of 36 participants will be randomly allocated into two groups using a sealed opaque envelope method. The Pilates breathing group and diaphragmatic breathing group will receive supervised breathing exercises for 2 consecutive days, with three sessions per day, in addition to routine care. brief_summary:
Background: Patients with breast cancer (BC) seem to have a higher prevalence of thyroid autoimmunity (TA), and this association has a solid pathogenic rationale: 1) I have discovered that BC tissue expresses thyroid peroxidase (TPO), a major thyroid autoantigen which exists in different isoforms by alternative splicing; 2) the immune system has a key role in both autoimmunity and cancer; 3) immunity and gut microbiota are deeply connected. Serum anti-TPO autoantibodies (TPOAb), the hallmark of TA, are highly prevalent among BC patients and they are associated with a better BC prognosis is retrospective studies. The magnitude of the relationship between BC and TA needs to be defined in longitudinal studies, unbiased by concurrent anti-cancer treatments.

Hypothesis: Patients with both BC and TA have a better BC prognosis, since they express intra-tumoral breast-specific TPO isoforms that are related with TPO-specific immune responses, and microbiota patterns, that contrast neoplastic progression, not present in patients affected with only BC and not associated TA.

Aims: 1) To verify the prevalence and prognostic impact of TA in the first unbiased longitudinal cohort of BC patients, recruited before anti-cancer treatments; 2) To investigate breast-specific TPO isoforms expression in BC tissue; 3) to characterise TPO-specific tissue-resident immune responses in paired human samples derived from BC and thyroid-related tissues/organs; 4) to explore the gut microbiota associated with BC and TA.

Experimental design: Monocentric 5-year longitudinal study. BC patients and non-cancer controls will be sampled from paired blood, stool, tumoral-breast samples (BC only), and neck lymph nodes (LNs). LNs contain thyroid-draining lymphocytes and are easily accessible by ultrasound-guided fine-needle-aspiration, a well-tolerated technique which I routinely operate for research purposes. Methods used to address aims: 1) Serum thyroid function and TPOAb measurement to assess TA; 2) RT-PCR amplification and product sequencing of tumor-derived RNA in BC patients, to identify TPO isoforms expression; 3) Flow-cytometry immunophenotyping of TPO-specific lymphocytes; 4) Metagenomics, metabolomics and metaproteomics for microbiota analysis.

Expected results: BC patients have a higher prevalence of TA than non-cancer controls (Aim 1A). Compared with BC-only patients, those affected with both BC and TA have a better 5-year prognosis (Aim 1B), express breast-specific TPO isoforms (Aim 2), have increased tumor-infiltrating and neck-LN-resident TPO-specific lymphocytes with anti-neoplastic activity, i.e. T follicular helper cells (Tfh) (Aim 3), and show peculiar microbiota signatures (Aim 4).

Impact on cancer: This study will clarify the prognostic role of TA in BC patients by combining paired clinical data, intra-tumoral antigen-expression and related lymphocytic infiltration, and microbiota patterns, generating novel clinical and therapeutic potential applications. Serum thyroid function and TPOAb, as well as intra-tumoral TPO isoforms, may be assessed as routine BC markers. Precision immunotherapy for BC may target TPO isoforms; the benefits of improved tumor control would likely overweight the downside of thyroid adverse effects, easily manageable with levothyroxine replacement treatment. The immune cell subsets identified in this study may suggest other immunotherapies for BC. Finally, future clinical trials of probiotics, antibiotics, or fecal material transplant, may be designed to target the microbiota signatures of BC patients with and without TA.

brief_summary:
Septic shock is a life-threatening condition caused by severe infection that leads to dangerously low blood pressure and impaired blood flow to body tissues and organs. In the intensive care unit (ICU), restoring adequate tissue perfusion (blood flow) is essential during resuscitation. While doctors routinely monitor overall blood pressure, microcirculatory blood flow in peripheral tissues, such as the skin of the feet, can remain poor even after general blood pressure targets are reached. The difference between core body temperature and big-toe skin temperature (known as the core-to-big-toe temperature gradient, or ΔT) reflects blood vessel constriction in the extremities. When peripheral blood flow improves, skin temperature rises and this gradient narrows.

This prospective observational study aims to evaluate whether serial measurements of the core-to-big-toe temperature gradient significantly change during the first 12 hours of ICU resuscitation in adult patients presenting with septic shock. The study also examines whether changes in this gradient correlate with standard indicators of clinical recovery, including blood pressure, vasopressor medicine requirements, and blood lactate clearance.

All enrolled participants will receive standard, evidence-based medical care for septic shock in accordance with current international clinical guidelines; study participation will not interfere with, alter, or delay clinical treatment. Non-invasive measurements will be collected at three time points: at ICU admission (Hour 0), at 6 hours, and at 12 hours. These assessments include core body temperature, big-toe skin temperature measured with a calibrated infrared thermometer, finger capillary refill time, routine arterial blood pressure, and arterial blood lactate levels. If effective, this temperature gradient could provide clinicians with a simple, non-invasive, and cost-effective bedside indicator to monitor peripheral perfusion during critical care resuscitation.
primary_outcomes: Change in Core-to-Big-Toe Temperature Gradient (ΔT) From Baseline to 12 Hours
title: Core-to-Big-Toe Temperature Gradient as a Marker of Peripheral Perfusion in Adult Patients With Septic Shock

brief_summary:
Introduction Despite advances in medical care, foreign body aspiration remains a common and ongoing health concern in children. Diagnostic bronchoscopy is the gold standard for confirming the diagnosis and providing definitive treatment. However, bronchoscopy performed for suspected foreign body aspiration in children yields negative findings in 16-57% of cases. Furthermore, oxygenation problems may occur during bronchoscopy performed under general anesthesia for foreign body aspiration. Respiratory complications requiring intensive care monitoring may develop in 6.3% of patients following bronchoscopy. These risks underscore the importance of preoperative assessment. In children with suspected foreign body aspiration, preoperative nasal capnography may complement clinical and radiological findings in determining the indications for bronchoscopy and predicting potential intraoperative complications.

Capnography assesses oxygenation status by measuring end-tidal carbon dioxide concentrations. Nasal capnography is used particularly during sedation and analgesia when spontaneous breathing is maintained. In patients scheduled for diagnostic bronchoscopy for suspected foreign body aspiration, preoperative capnographic assessment may help predict complications occurring during and after the procedure.

This study aims to evaluate the association of preoperative nasal capnographic measurements with positive and negative bronchoscopic findings and potential intraoperative complications in children with foreign body aspiration.

Methods Ethical approval was obtained from the Mersin University Health Sciences Ethics Committee (2026/556). The study, including data collection, is planned to be completed within 12 months of ethical approval. The ethics application stated that an application for project funding would be submitted to the Mersin University Scientific Research Projects (BAP) Unit. The study period was specified in the ethics application as one year following approval by the BAP Unit. Data collection will commence after the nasal capnography device has been procured through the project.

Children aged 0-18 years undergoing rigid bronchoscopy for foreign body aspiration at the Department of Pediatric Surgery, Mersin University Hospital, during the specified study period will be eligible for inclusion. Patients operated on by Associate Professor Caner İsbir, Dr. Hatice Büyüköztürk Çolak, or Dr. Mert Jundi will be included. All investigators will participate in data collection, and the collected data will be analyzed by Associate Professor Caner İsbir and Dr. Hatice Büyüköztürk Çolak.

Patients presenting with foreign body aspiration during the study period will be excluded if they decline rigid bronchoscopy, if their legal guardians do not sign the study-specific informed consent forms, or if nasal capnographic measurements cannot be recorded because of technical difficulties.

In patients admitted to the pediatric surgery ward with suspected foreign body aspiration, end-tidal carbon dioxide (ETCO₂) will be measured using a capnography device connected to a nasal cannula during preoperative preparation on the ward, before rigid bronchoscopy. Measurements will be recorded numerically for each patient. ETCO₂ values will also be classified into two groups: values up to and including the 35-45 mmHg range and values above this range.

The following variables will be assessed: age, sex, body weight, weight percentiles, preoperative pulse oximetry readings, preoperative clinical symptoms, physical examination findings, radiological findings, and postoperative complications following bronchoscopy. Patients will be categorized into three age groups: 0-6, 6-12, and 12-18 years.

The associations between nasal capnographic measurements and positive or negative bronchoscopic findings, as well as intraoperative and postoperative complications, will be examined. Independent-samples t-tests and chi-square tests will be used to assess the associations of preoperative capnographic measurements with bronchoscopic findings and intraoperative and postoperative complications. Logistic regression analysis will additionally be used to examine the associations of nasal capnographic measurements within the specified age groups with positive or negative bronchoscopic findings and intraoperative and postoperative complications.
primary_outcomes: Measurement of end-tidal carbon dioxide levels using a nasal capnography device
Enhancing safety in diagnostic bronchoscopy for foreign body aspiration in children
title: The Impact of Preoperative Nasal Capnography on Clinical Management in Patients Undergoing Diagnostic Bronchoscopy for Suspected Foreign Body Aspiration

brief_summary:
The purpose of this study is to evaluate the impact of a training intervention aimed at nursing personnel on the appropriateness of the indication of long peripheral venous catheters in candidate pediatric and neonatal patients, comparing the clinical practice of nursing personnel before and after the intervention.

Study Design: Prospective, unicentric quality improvement study.

The study consists of three phases:

1. -Pre-intervention phase: prospective collection of data from routine clinical practice, with a descriptive character, in relation to the use of catheters Venous short peripheral and long.
2. -Educational intervention: structured training directed to nursing staff about indications, technique and care of the catheters Venous long peripherals, including specific training in the ultrasound assessment of the venous tree as a support tool for the selection of the most suitable vein for the cannulation of the catheter.
3. -Post-intervention phase: protocol implementation of use of catheters Venous Long peripherals and prospective data collection of all peripheral venous accesses (short and long) in order to evaluate changes in clinical practice and results after the intervention. Likewise, the post-intervention phase will include a follow-up period with the objective of evaluating the sustainability of the effects of the intervention over time.

The collection of data over a prolonged period is contemplated, can be extended up to 24 months after the intervention, to analyze the maintenance of the adequacy in the indication of peripheral venous catheters, the incidence of complications and the stability of the clinical results. In a complementary way, the maintenance of the knowledge acquired by the nursing staff and the adherence to the protocol in routine clinical practice will be assessed.

Study Population and Total Number of Patients: The study population is structured in two levels: professional population (intervention) and clinical population (pre- and post-intervention).

1. Professional population (intervention phase) The study population corresponding to the intervention phase will consist of the group of nursing professionals of the Pediatric and Neonatology Service of the Jiménez Díaz Foundation University Hospital , who participate in the training intervention on ultrasound vascular assessment, channeling of long peripheral venous catheters and implementation of the care protocol.

   The service has a care staff of 21 nursing professionals (approximately 3 to 5 per shift), distributed among the pediatric hospitalization floor, Pediatric Intensive Care Unit (PICU) and Neonatology Unit.

   Regarding their characteristics, the age of the professionals is approximately between 25 and 50 years, with an estimated average of around 35-40 years. Professional seniority varies between approximately 1 and 30 years of experience.

   The training intervention will be offered to all staff of the Pediatric Service, although participation will be voluntary, so no sample calculation is established at this stage.

   The following will be evaluated for this population:
   * Knowledge before and after training.
   * Satisfaction with training.
   * Satisfaction with the use of long peripheral venous catheters.
   * Adherence to the implemented protocol.
2. Clinical population: Hospitalized pediatric patients will be included, from birth to 17 years of age, admitted to the pediatric hospitalization unit, the PICU and the Neonatology Unit, who are expected to require intravenous treatment by peripheral line for more than three days and whose parents or legal guardians give informed consent to participate and informed assent in the case of patients older than 12 years.

Schedule and Expected Date of Completion: The study is expected to begin in September 2026 , subject to obtaining approval from the Research Ethics Committee. The development period of the study will extend until October 2028 , including the preparation phase, the collection of pre-intervention data, the implementation of the training intervention and the subsequent follow-up of the participants and pediatric and neonatal patients. The study includes a short-, medium- and long-term follow-up, as well as the closing phase, data analysis and writing of the final report. These dates are estimates and could be adjusted according to the evolution of data collection and clinical follow-up.

This single-center, randomized, double-blind, crossover clinical trial aims to compare the volumetric visual fields provided by two occupational progressive addition lenses (OPLs) optimized for intermediate and near vision in presbyopic patients. The study evaluates Vimax PC 1.5 FWD 133 cm and Vimax PC 1.5 FWD 200 cm lenses and Vimax Fit FRM, all of them with plano distance power and a +2.00 D near addition, in order to determine differences in the extent of clear vision at multiple working distances.

Participants will undergo a comprehensive optometric examination including medical and ocular history, visual acuity assessment, accommodative amplitude measurement, autorefraction, interpupillary distance measurement, ocular motility evaluation, confrontation visual fields, Amsler grid testing, and binocular vision assessment. Visual field measurements will then be performed using both study lenses under standardized conditions. Subjects will be instructed to maintain a fixed head position while identifying optotypes located at distances of 4 m, 2 m, 1.33 m, 80 cm, 40 cm, and 25 cm. Both lenses will be tested in random order under masked conditions so that neither participants nor investigators know which lens design is being evaluated during each phase.

At least 23 presbyopic participants are expected to be enrolled. The study procedures are non-invasive and are anticipated to be completed in a single one-hour visit, although additional sessions may be scheduled if necessary. No significant risks are expected beyond possible transient visual fatigue associated with the duration of testing.

The primary objective is to determine which occupational progressive lens design provides a greater spatial volume of clear vision and wider horizontal and vertical visual fields at different intermediate and near distances. The findings may contribute to improving personalized recommendations of occupational lenses according to patients' visual demands and working distances.
primary_outcomes: Visual field volume
title: Volumetric Visual Fields at Different Distances in Presbyopic Patients Using Occupational (PC-133 and PC-200) and General-Purpose Progressive Addition Lenses

brief_summary: IBO-CARE is a single-site Phase 1/2a study evaluating the safety, tolerability, feasibility and preliminary outcomes of medically supervised ibogaine with 12 months of recovery support in adults with moderate-to-severe opioid use disorder. Up to 120 candidates will be screened to enrol 60 adults aged 18-65 into three cohorts of 20. Participants meeting the shared opioid-free and negative naloxone-challenge criteria will be randomised 1:1 to Cohort A or Cohort C. Cohort A receives extended-release naltrexone 380 mg intramuscularly and matching oral placebo. Cohort C receives oral ibogaine hydrochloride and matching intramuscular placebo. Cohort B follows a separate, nonrandomised recent-use ibogaine pathway with matching intramuscular placebo and clinically supervised stabilisation. All cohorts attend three monitored oral-treatment admissions at Months 0, 1 and 2. Repeat ibogaine administrations require individual eligibility and safety release. The planned injection schedule comprises twelve calendar-monthly administrations at Months 0-11, with final follow-up at Month 12. All participants receive equivalent preparation, psychological support, continuing addiction care, monthly clinical review and SENTINEL digital recovery support with a Garmin Venu 4. The acute monitoring model includes continuous telemetry during a 72-hour post-dose window, serial 12-lead ECGs, laboratory monitoring, emergency capability and independent safety oversight. Monitoring is extended when clinically required. Wearable information does not replace clinical cardiac monitoring. SENTINEL combines participant reports, wearable trends and scheduled assessments, with high-risk findings reviewed by qualified clinicians. Cohorts A and C use a double-blind, double-dummy comparison. Cohort B is open to the treating team, with masked outcome assessment where feasible. Treatment guesses are collected because the acute effects of ibogaine may reveal allocation. The study estimates preliminary effects and is not designed to establish confirmatory efficacy. The IND application has not yet been filed. The study remains not yet recruiting. ClinicalTrials.gov registration and assignment of an NCT number do not authorise study conduct. Enrolment and investigational treatment will begin only after the IND is in effect, IRB approval is in place, and all applicable DEA, Colorado, investigational-product, clinical-site and digital-system requirements have been satisfied. The registration will be updated when the actual FDA filing details are available.

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical study is to learn whether the GastricOn 6-Month Gastric Balloon helps adults with obesity lose weight, and how safe it is. The GastricOn balloon is a soft, temporary device that is placed in the stomach through the mouth using an endoscope (a thin, flexible tube with a camera), without surgery. Once in place, it is filled with saline (salt water). By taking up space in the stomach, it helps people feel full sooner and eat less. The balloon stays in the stomach for about 6 months and is then removed the same way.

The main questions this study aims to answer are:

How much of their total body weight do participants lose 26 weeks after the balloon is placed? How often do serious side effects related to the device or the procedure occur?

Researchers will also look at changes in body mass index (BMI), excess weight loss, appetite, eating habits and participant satisfaction.

About 70 adults aged 18 to 60 years with a BMI between 30 and 40 kg/m² will take part at 3 hospitals in Türkiye. All participants will receive the balloon; there is no comparison group.

Participants will:

Have screening tests, including a physical exam, blood tests and an endoscopy of the stomach Have the balloon placed under light sedation and stay for observation for 1 to 2 hours before going home Take a stomach acid-reducing medicine (proton pump inhibitor) while the balloon is in place Follow a supervised diet and lifestyle program Attend follow-up visits on Day 7 and at Weeks 4, 12, 24 and 26, where their weight is measured, side effects are checked and questionnaires are completed Have the balloon removed under light sedation at Week 24

Participants will have access to a 24/7 advice line during the study.
primary_outcomes: Percentage of Total Body Weight Loss (%TBWL)
Incidence of Device- and Procedure-Related Serious Adverse Events (SAEs)

brief_summary:
This study tests whether an artificial intelligence (AI) tool helps radiologists read X-rays more accurately.

Radiologists read X-rays to find diseases such as pneumonia, bone fractures, and abdominal problems. AI is a computer program trained on many past X-rays. It may help radiologists spot diseases faster and more correctly. This study compares reading X-rays with the AI tool to reading X-rays without it.

Who takes part

* Ten radiologists from several hospitals.
* X-ray images from about 300 to 500 past hospital visits.
* No new X-rays are taken.
* All names and ID numbers are removed from the images.

What happens

* Each radiologist reads the same set of X-rays twice.
* One time, the radiologist reads without the AI tool.
* The other time, the radiologist can see the AI result.
* Half start with no AI and then switch to AI. The other half start with AI and then switch to no AI.
* There is a four-week break between the two times.
* The researchers measure how accurate each radiologist is. They also time how long each image takes.

Possible benefits and risks

* The radiologists may get no direct personal benefit.
* The results may show whether AI can help doctors read X-rays better in the future.
* This is a low-risk study. The AI tool never tells a patient a diagnosis directly.
* A qualified radiologist always makes the final diagnosis.
* Patient data is stored on a locked, encrypted server.
lead_sponsor: The Third Affiliated Hospital of Southern Medical University
primary_outcomes: The disease exists / does not exist
title: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence-Assisted X-ray Interpretation on Radiologists' Diagnostic Performance

brief_summary:
Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is a multisystemic disorder with metabolic and endocrine implications, commonly observed in women of reproductive age and characterized by hyperandrogenism, ovulatory dysfunction, and polycystic ovarian morphology. Insulin resistance, chronic low-grade inflammation, hormonal imbalances, and obesity can contribute to reduced cardiorespiratory fitness and muscular endurance, in addition to the metabolic complications associated with PCOS. Furthermore, psychosocial effects such as depression, anxiety, and impaired quality of life may also occur. Lifestyle modifications and exercise are among the first-line approaches in the management of PCOS. Aerobic and resistance exercises have been reported to have positive effects on insulin resistance, cardiometabolic risk factors, hormonal profiles, inflammation, body composition, and reproductive functions. However, evidence regarding the specific effects of different exercise modalities on physical fitness components-such as cardiovascular and muscular endurance, which are adversely affected in PCOS-remains limited. Spinal stabilization exercises constitute an exercise approach aimed at enhancing core muscle strength and endurance, postural control, and movement quality by targeting deep trunk muscle activation, lumbopelvic stability, and neuromuscular control. Although studies exist regarding Pilates interventions targeting the core region in individuals with PCOS, no study has been found that examines the effects of spinal stabilization exercises administered either in isolation or as an adjunct to aerobic exercise. Therefore, it is hypothesized that incorporating spinal stabilization exercises into an aerobic exercise regimen may provide additional benefits-particularly regarding metabolic, hormonal, and inflammatory outcomes, alongside physical fitness components.

The aim of this study is to comparatively examine the effects of spinal stabilization exercises added to aerobic exercise-versus aerobic exercise alone-on metabolic, hormonal, and inflammatory markers, anthropometric characteristics, cardiovascular fitness, core muscle strength and endurance, and quality of life in individuals with PCOS.
primary_outcomes: Fasting Blood Glucose Concentration
title: Investigation of the Effectiveness of Spinal Stabilization Exercises Added to Aerobic Exercise in Women With Polycystic Ovary Syndrome

brief_summary:
Acute pulmonary embolism (PE) is a serious and potentially life-threatening condition in which blood clots block the arteries of the lungs. For patients with intermediate-high-risk PE, doctors may remove the clots through a thin tube (catheter) placed into the lung arteries, a procedure called percutaneous catheter aspiration.

Two main types of catheters are used. Small-bore catheters (8-12 French) are easier to guide into the smaller, more distant branches of the lung arteries, but they remove large central clots less efficiently. Large-bore catheters (16 French or larger) remove central clots more effectively, but are harder to advance into the smaller branches. Some doctors use both types together, starting with a large-bore catheter for the central clot and then a small-bore catheter for the remaining distal clot. It is not yet known which of these three approaches is safest and works best.

This study will follow about 225 adults with intermediate-high-risk acute PE who are treated with catheter aspiration at five hospitals in China. Participants are grouped according to the catheter strategy that was actually used during their routine care: small-bore aspiration only, large-bore aspiration only, or combined large-bore plus small-bore aspiration. Information is collected from routine hospital tests, CT scans, echocardiograms, procedure records, and follow-up visits at 24 hours, 48 hours, 7 days, 30 days, and 90 days after the procedure. The study does not require any extra invasive tests or procedures.

The main goals are to compare, among the three groups: (1) the rate of major adverse events within 7 days after the procedure, and (2) the improvement in right-heart strain seen on CT scans 48 hours after the procedure. The results may help doctors choose the most suitable catheter strategy for patients with intermediate-high-risk acute PE.
interventions: Large-bore (16 F or larger) percutaneous catheter aspiration thrombectomy
Combined large-bore and small-bore percutaneous catheter aspiration
primary_outcomes: Composite Major Adverse Events Within 7 Days After the Procedure
Change in Right Ventricular to Left Ventricular (RV/LV) Diameter Ratio on CTPA From Baseline to 48 Hours After the Procedure
title: Comparing Three Catheter Aspiration Strategies for Intermediate-High-Risk Acute Pulmonary Embolism

brief_summary:
This study compares two methods for assessing carotid artery plaques - deposits of cholesterol and other substances that can build up in the neck arteries and potentially lead to stroke. The first method, Carotid Plaque RADS, is a standardized ultrasound-based scoring system where expert physicians visually classify plaques into categories reflecting their stability. The second method, CPVH (Carotid Plaque Virtual Histopathology), is a software tool that automatically analyzes ultrasound images to identify plaque components (lipids, fibrous tissue, calcium, blood, muscle) and calculates a prognostic index indicating plaque vulnerability.

The study aims to determine how well the results of these two methods agree with each other, whether they identify the same plaques as unstable or vulnerable, and how well each method predicts clinical outcomes such as transient ischemic attack (TIA), ischemic stroke, progression of arterial narrowing, or the need for surgery (carotid endarterectomy or stenting) within a 12-month follow-up period.

Patients with carotid atherosclerotic plaques of any degree of severity are included. Plaques are evaluated independently by three ultrasound experts using the Carotid Plaque RADS system and separately by the CPVH software. The results are compared across four groups based on the degree of arterial narrowing: less than 20%, 20-49%, 50-69%, and 70-99%. The study also identifies cases where the two methods disagree and analyzes possible reasons for these discrepancies.

The findings are expected to provide practical recommendations for combining both methods in clinical practice, to improve the identification of high-risk plaques and to help personalize treatment decisions for patients with carotid atherosclerosis.
interventions: Carotid Ultrasound with CPVH and Carotid Plaque RADS Assessment

primary_outcomes: Agreement between Carotid Plaque RADS and CPVH Prognostic Index
title: Carotid Plaque RADS vs CPVH: Diagnostic Accuracy Comparison

Hearing loss and cognitive impairment are common and interrelated health problems that may affect communication, information processing, attention, psychological well-being, daily functioning, and quality of life. This study aims to develop and evaluate a comorbidity-oriented Auditory-Cognitive Optimization Care Program (A-COP) for individuals with hearing loss and cognitive impairment.

The A-COP will be developed based on evidence from a literature review and findings from qualitative research involving individuals with hearing loss and cognitive impairment and their caregivers. The program integrates hearing-related care and cognitive stimulation strategies to address the combined needs associated with hearing and cognitive difficulties.

In the intervention phase, participants will be randomly assigned to either the A-COP intervention group or an active control group in a two-arm, parallel-group randomized controlled trial. The study will evaluate changes in cognitive function, hearing and communication-related outcomes, depressive symptoms, and quality of life from baseline through the 6-month follow-up. The findings will provide evidence regarding the effects of the A-COP in individuals with hearing loss and cognitive impairment.
primary_outcomes: Global Cognitive Function
Executive Function
Working Memory
title: Auditory-Cognitive Optimization Care Program for Older Adults With Hearing Loss and Cognitive Impairment

The study will include 100 adults undergoing planned hand, wrist, or forearm surgery at Ankara Bilkent City Hospital. Researchers will compare 50 participants with a BMI below 30 kg/m² and 50 participants with a BMI of 30 kg/m² or higher.

The study will assess the time needed to perform the block, block success, the time until sensation and movement are blocked, and patient satisfaction. Researchers will also examine whether arm circumference and muscle measurements are associated with block outcomes.

This is an observational study. Participants will receive routine anesthesia and surgical care, and their treatment will not be assigned or changed for research purposes.

The study is a prospective, randomized, single-blind, active-controlled, non-inferiority trial enrolling 150 participants, who will receive a single intra-articular injection of either TrHCROSS® or a reference viscosupplement and will be followed for 12 months. The primary effectiveness endpoint is pain reduction at 24 weeks, while safety will be assessed through the incidence of treatment-related serious adverse events.

Secondary and exploratory assessments will evaluate changes in pain, joint function, mobility, quality of life, patient satisfaction, investigator global assessment, rescue medication use, and the occurrence of adverse events over 52 weeks. Outcomes will be measured using validated, joint-specific instruments, including WOMAC and KOOS for knee osteoarthritis, WOMAC and HOOS for hip osteoarthritis, and SPADI and WOSI for shoulder osteoarthritis. The results of this investigation are intended to generate post-market clinical evidence supporting the safety and clinical performance of TrHCROSS® across different joint indications and to further characterize its benefit-risk profile in routine clinical practice.

brief_summary:
Medical education increasingly emphasizes individualized learning and formative assessment; however, providing timely and personalized feedback to students remains challenging because of limited faculty resources. Generative artificial intelligence (AI) may provide a scalable approach for generating individualized feedback based on students' learning needs, but its educational effectiveness compared with traditional feedback approaches remains uncertain.

This study is a single-center, prospective, three-arm, cluster randomized controlled trial designed to evaluate the effect of pretest-based individualized feedback on medical students' learning outcomes during a nephrology clerkship. Undergraduate medical students participating in a nephrology clerkship at The Second Qilu Hospital of Shandong University will be recruited and assigned by teaching class clusters to one of three groups: an AI-generated feedback group, a rule-based individualized feedback group, or a no-feedback control group.

All participants will receive the same nephrology clerkship teaching based on the BOPPPS-CBL instructional model. Before the clerkship, students will complete a diagnostic pretest. Based on the pretest results, individualized feedback will be provided according to group allocation. The primary outcome is immediate knowledge acquisition assessed by the post-test score immediately after the clerkship. Secondary outcomes include four-week knowledge retention, knowledge gap remediation, and clinical reasoning performance.

This study aims to determine whether AI-generated individualized feedback provides additional educational benefits compared with traditional rule-based feedback and no feedback, and to provide evidence for the application of artificial intelligence-assisted personalized learning in medical education.
primary_outcomes: Immediate Knowledge Acquisition
title: AI-Generated and Rule-Based Individualized Feedback for Medical Students' Nephrology Learning

brief_summary:
Advanced cancer is a leading cause of death worldwide and in China. Cancer patients often face reduced independence and self-care abilities, which may lead to psychological disturbances such as helplessness, hopelessness, or meaninglessness. This combination of these negative emotions is called demoralization. Approximately 35.8% of cancer patients experience demoralization, with higher rates in terminal stages. If unrecognized or untreated, it can increase physical and mental symptom burden, reduce quality of life, and even lead to suicide. To date, no professional bodies currently recommend treatment guidelines. One meta-analysis suggests that psychological interventions could significantly reduce demoralization; however, the requirement for in-person attendance may create accessibility challenges, potentially reducing the flexibility and acceptability of psychological interventions for cancer patients undergoing chemotherapy or receiving treatment at home.

To address the identified literature gap, a co-designed digital psychological intervention was developed, and this study will evaluate its feasibility. A convenience sample of 30 advanced cancer patients meeting the inclusion criteria will be recruited from the oncology ward of a hospital in Shenzhen. Participants will receive five 30-45 minute sessions of a co-designed, digitally-enabled positive psychological intervention, delivered weekly over five weeks. A trained researcher will introduce the intervention before discharge and deliver it through a WeChat Mini Program in the patients' homes. The primary outcome will be feasibility (time to complete recruitment, eligibility rate, recruitment rate, retention rate, attendance rate, and acceptability rate). Secondary outcomes will be measured for preliminary intervention effectiveness on demoralization, suicidal ideation, and quality of life of advanced cancer patients at baseline (after collecting demographic information and written consent forms) and post-intervention. A separate researcher will conduct a descriptive qualitative evaluation with 12 participants to explore their experience of the intervention. Qualitative data will be audio-taped, transcribed verbatim, and analyzed using NVivo 14 through thematic analysis. Quantitative data will be entered into SPSS version 29.0. Descriptive statistics will be used to summarize the profiles of participants and outcomes.
interventions: A digitally-enabled positive psychological intervention for demoralization in advanced cancer patients

Feasibility outcome: eligibility rate
Feasibility outcome: recruitment rate
Feasibility outcome: retention rate
Feasibility outcome: attendance rate
Acceptability outcome: participants' satisfaction and perspectives of the intervention
Qualitative evaluation of acceptability
title: A Feasibility Study of a Digitally-enabled Psychological Intervention for Demoralization in Advanced Cancer Patients

The study will also examine hospitalizations and emergency room visits, cognitive function, caregiver burden, quality of life, satisfaction, and changes in medication-management behavior. The study is intended to determine whether HomeCare can improve medication management and support both people living with dementia and their caregivers.

brief_summary:
The aim of this study is to evaluate the effects of sleep quality on cardiovascular disease risk and food and nutrient intakes. Within the scope of this study, several parameters associated with cardiovascular disease risk will be assessed, including waist circumference, hip circumference, waist-to-hip ratio, waist-to-height ratio, triceps skinfold thickness, mid-upper arm circumference, and serum levels of glucose, HbA1c, insulin, LDL cholesterol, HDL cholesterol, total cholesterol, homocysteine, and lipoprotein(a). Cardiovascular disease risk will be evaluated using the Framingham Risk Score, SCORE2, and A Body Shape Index (ABSI).

To assess visceral adiposity, a formula incorporating waist circumference and serum triglyceride and HDL cholesterol levels will be used. In addition, participants' body fat and muscle percentages will be determined. Carbohydrate, fat, protein, vitamin, mineral, and fluid intakes will also be compared between individuals with poor and good sleep quality, and the effects of sleep quality on nutrient intake will be evaluated.

Previous studies investigating the effects of sleep quality on diabetes or cardiovascular diseases have predominantly been conducted among middle-aged adults aged 50 years and older, a population with a higher prevalence of dysglycemia, dyslipidemia, and hypertension. In the present project, all eligible adults aged 18 years and older will be evaluated. Furthermore, to our knowledge, no previous study has comprehensively evaluated the effects of sleep quality on cardiovascular disease risk together with nutrient intakes among individuals with type 2 diabetes.

This study is expected to contribute to the literature by evaluating the effects of sleep quality on cardiovascular disease risk among individuals with type 2 diabetes. In addition, the extent to which sleep quality is associated with dietary habits will be examined at the level of nutrient intake. brief_summary:
This is a dose-ranging, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled 12-week Phase 2a trial with an up to two week loading dose period. Eligible participants will be sequentially randomized 3:1 into three parallel groups, low-dose, mid-dose, and high-dose, to receive GV101 or placebo once daily for 12 weeks.

The low-dose group will receive 200 mg from Weeks 2-12 after a 100 mg loading dose at Week 1; the mid-dose group will receive 300 mg from Weeks 3-12 after loading doses of 100 mg and 200 mg at Weeks 1 and 2, respectively; and the high dose group will receive 400 mg from Weeks 3-12 after loading doses of 200 mg and 300 mg at Weeks 1 and 2, respectively. Target enrollment is 16 participants per dose group. The primary efficacy endpoint at 12 weeks is percent change in blood FXN-M protein in each dose group compared with placebo, the key secondary endpoints are change in hs-cTnI and mFARS score in each dose group compared with placebo. Data for exploratory, safety, PK, and PD endpoints will also be collected and analyzed.

Down-dosing will be allowed in groups dosed with \> 200 mg daily. Participants who complete the 12-week trial are eligible to continue into a 52-week OLE at 200 mg until the first participant from the second dose group completes the 12-week trial, at which time all OLE participants will be asked to increase their dose (4-week window) to 300 mg per day. When the first participant from the third dose group completes the 12-week trial, all current OLE participants will be asked to increase their dose (4-week window) to 400 mg per day. Participants in the second dose group will start the OLE with a 1 week loading dose of 200 mg per day and be asked to increase to 300 mg per day after the first week. Participants in the third dose group will start the OLE with a 1 week loading dose of 200 mg per day and will be asked to increase to 300 mg per day after the first week and to 400 mg per day after the second week.

The OLE extends initially for 52 weeks from the last participant's entry; an additional OLE or expanded access is anticipated after this OLE to provide seamless treatment until program cessation or drug approval. Safety and efficacy assessment will continue throughout the dosing period. Down dosing related to tolerance is allowed during the OLE.

title: GV101 for Friedreich's Ataxia (FA) Treatment

Ongoing psychological stress is known to affect immune function and increase inflammation in the body. This study will investigate whether a daily jelly containing alginate support gut health and improve immune responses compared to a placebo in adults experiencing higher levels of chronic stress.

We are recruiting participants with elevated chronic stress to assess whether a functional jelly containing alginate, can help to reduce markers of inflammation, by mediating a change in gut microbiota composition.

brief_summary:
The treatment of dementias of neurodegenerative origin is currently limited to symptomatic drugs that are unable to interfere with the underlying mechanisms of neurodegeneration, as the pathological processes leading to dementia begin decades before the onset of clinical symptoms. In this context, biomarkers for the diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease (AD), the most common form of dementia, are currently available but are either invasive, requiring lumbar puncture, or very expensive, such as PET imaging with amyloid and, potentially, tau tracers. Their widespread application across different clinical settings is therefore impractical.

Accordingly, one of the major challenges in this field is the identification of peripheral screening biomarkers with a high negative predictive value (NPV), capable of identifying individuals who are negative for disease-associated biomarkers and can therefore be classified as healthy. Among the most promising biomarkers for neurodegenerative diseases are microRNAs (miRNAs), small non-coding RNA molecules.

This study is part of the Italian National Recovery and Resilience Plan (PNRR) project on high-impact Non-Communicable Chronic Diseases (MCnT2), Project Code PNRR-POC-2023-12377354, funded by the Italian Ministry of Health/European Union - Next Generation EU - PNRR M6C2, Investment 2.1, "Enhancement and Strengthening of Biomedical Research within the Italian National Health Service." The participating institutions are Fondazione IRCCS Ca' Granda Ospedale Maggiore Policlinico di Milano and Azienda Ospedaliero-Universitaria "Policlinico San Marco" di Catania.

The main working hypotheses of the funded PNRR project are the identification of miRNAs that are dysregulated in patients with AD compared with age-matched healthy individuals and patients with non-AD conditions, and the development of a solution-based sensor for the simplified detection of the identified miRNAs. The sensor will exploit the biochemical methodology developed in Italian Patent No. IT102022000014740 (filed on July 13, 2022), which is capable of measuring the levels of specific enzymes in saliva.

The project is structured into three Work Packages (WPs):

WP1: Identification and validation of candidate miRNAs and calculation of their negative predictive value (NPV).

WP2: Development and optimization of the solution-based sensor and assessment of its ability to detect the findings identified in WP1 using a simpler methodology.

WP3: Testing of the sensor in a cohort of patients with AD and controls across different clinical settings, including neurological and dental clinics, in order to assess its applicability in real-world clinical practice.

In this study, we aim to:

identify the most significantly dysregulated miRNAs in the saliva of patients with AD (WP1); and develop and optimize a solution-based gold nanoparticle biosensor capable of detecting candidate miRNAs in saliva samples from both patients with AD and healthy individuals (WP2).
lead_sponsor: Fondazione IRCCS Ca' Granda, Ospedale Maggiore Policlinico
primary_outcomes: miRNAs identification
title: Functionalized Point of Care and 3D Printed Dental Aligners as Devices for Early Detection of Neurodegenerative Diseases

Sedation is routinely used during interventional endoscopic procedures to improve patient comfort and optimize procedural conditions. Non-anaesthesiologist-administered propofol sedation (NAPS) has been demonstrated to be safe and effective for many endoscopic procedures, including complex interventions such as endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP). However, evidence supporting its use during technically demanding or prolonged procedures and in patients with severe comorbidities (ASA class ≥ III) remains limited.

At our institution, interventional endoscopic procedures have been routinely performed for many years using standardized NAPS protocols, including in higher-risk patients, with comprehensive staff training, continuous patient monitoring, supplemental oxygen administration, and immediate access to an emergency response team. This non-interventional observational study will prospectively collect data on sedation practices, procedural characteristics, and sedation-related outcomes during routine interventional endoscopy without altering standard clinical care. Arthroscopic tenotomy of the long head of the biceps tendon is an established treatment for pain associated with massive irreparable rotator cuff tears, as supported by the available literature.

Radiofrequency ablation of the suprascapular nerve provides temporary pain control by destroying the sensory nerve fibres supplying the shoulder joint.

Tenotomy of the long head of the biceps tendon can be performed safely using a minimally invasive, ultrasound-guided outpatient procedure under local anaesthesia, without the general anaesthesia required for arthroscopy.

The aim of the study is to compare the reduction in pain intensity and the duration of analgesia following percutaneous tenotomy of the long head of the biceps tendon versus continuous radiofrequency ablation of the suprascapular nerve. Changes in shoulder mobility limitations following the two procedures will also be compared using the Constant-Murley score, which assesses shoulder function.

This study compares a wearable brain-computer interface (BCI) communication device with the eye-tracking communication devices that people with ALS already use.

As ALS progresses, speech is lost and many people come to rely on an eye-tracking speech generating device. Eye-tracking performance can decline as oculomotor control is affected, and some people reach a point where it no longer works reliably for them. The Cognixion ONE device adds a brain-computer interface input, which does not depend on eye movement, alongside an AI-assisted communication application.

Thirty adults with ALS who currently use a Tobii Dynavox or Smartbox eye-tracking device will take part. Each participant uses three communication options at home over a 12-week period: their own eye-tracking device, the Cognixion ONE device with a head-worn augmented-reality display, and the Cognixion ONE device with a screen-based display. For some sessions the option is assigned; for others the participant chooses.

The main measure is how much time participants voluntarily choose to spend using each option. That choice is treated as the clearest signal of which option genuinely works better for them. The study also measures communication speed and accuracy, usability, workload, quality of life, and caregiver burden.

The Cognixion ONE device is an investigational research device. It is not approved or cleared by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration for any medical use.
primary_outcomes: Voluntary daily use time per input modality
title: Brain-Computer Interface Communication Device for People With ALS

Patients scheduled to undergo suturing for minor trauma in the emergency department frequently experience anticipatory pain and anxiety before the procedure. These experiences may negatively affect perceived pain, cooperation with treatment, adherence, satisfaction, and the overall care experience. However, the realities of emergency department practice, including crowding, high patient volume, staff shortages, and increased workload, may limit effective nurse-patient communication and comprehensive patient education.

Patients awaiting suturing for minor trauma often experience uncertainty, prolonged waiting, fear of the procedure, and concern about pain. These factors may increase anxiety, which can further intensify pain perception and negatively influence patients' cooperation with treatment and satisfaction with care. Previous reports indicate that many patients waiting in emergency departments seek information about waiting times, care processes, and their medical conditions, highlighting a substantial need for accessible and reliable information.

During this waiting period, patients may increasingly use artificial intelligence-based digital resources to obtain information about their health condition and the procedure they are about to undergo. However, information generated by artificial intelligence may be inaccurate, incomplete, or insufficiently tailored to the clinical context. Therefore, such information should be reviewed and validated by healthcare professionals before being provided to patients.

This study aims to evaluate the effect of an artificial intelligence-assisted patient education material delivered during the pre-suturing waiting period on pain and anxiety levels among patients with minor trauma in the emergency department. It is also expected that the educational material developed within the scope of this study may contribute to patient education and supportive care in emergency department settings.

brief_summary:
Graves' disease (GD) is the commonest cause of hyperthyroidism, characterised by anti-thyrotropin receptor autoantibodies (TRAb) persistently stimulating the thyroid gland. Around 30-50% GD patients also develop Graves' orbitopathy (GO), an orbital inflammation causing disfigurement and visual problems; moderate-to-severe forms represent 5% of GO cases and are associated with high risk of sight loss. Some risk factors for GO have been identified (i.e. smoking, stress, high TRAb titres, severe hyperthyroidism) and predictive models for disease development and response to treatment have been attempted, but are still missing/incomplete. The GD/GO pathogenesis is multifactorial and not fully understood, including a complex interplay between genetic predisposition and environmental factors. A loss of immune tolerance has been observed; in particular an imbalance between T Helper 17 (Th17) and T Regulatory (Treg). The gut microbiota modulates the differentiation of immature T cells in the gut-associated-lymphoid-tissue and microbiota alterations seem involved in autoimmune diseases, including GD/GO. Indeed, a dysbiosis of the gut microbiota may alter the Treg/T17 balance and thus impact on immune homeostasis.

The international EU-FP7 funded study "Investigation of Novel biomarkers and Definition of the role of the microbiome In Graves' Orbitopathy" (INDIGO) represented one of the first investigations about the role of gut microbiota in GD and GO diseases (https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/612116), spanning across eight centres of four European countries: United Kingdom (Cardiff, Merthyr Tydfil, Newcastle upon Tyne and Moorfields), Italy (Milan and Pisa), Belgium (Brussels) and Germany (Essen). The INDIGO consortium provided the human gut microbiome analysis by 16S rRNA sequencing, performed on faecal samples of 105 patients (59 GD, 46 GO) and 41 controls enrolled between October 2014 and June 2016. It was discovered an increase of Actinobacteria phylum in both GD and GO compared with controls, and a selective enrichment of Roseburia spp. in moderate-severe GO compared with both GD and controls.

The first objective of this MISS.GO study is to validate with advanced metagenomics techniques (Shotgun sequencing) the INDIGO study's gut microbiome findings, whose samples were stored in a biobank of UO1 (UNIMI). The Shotgun sequencing allows a deeper taxonomic investigation down to species level, while 16s rRNA sequencing is limited to genus level. Furthermore it increases the chances to detect low abundant species, not possible with 16S rRNA sequencing, and extends the microbiome analysis to yeasts, fungi and a variety of other microorganisms in addition to Bacteria and Archea, to which 16s rRNA sequencing is restricted. Furthermore, this study integrates the metabolomics analysis performed on stored plasma of INDIGO's patients.

The MISS.GO study also includes a prospective phase were 59 subjects (33 GO, 9 GD and 17 controls) were recruited in the Fondazione IRCCS Ca' Granda Ospedale Maggiore Policlinico of Milan, Italy, to deliver an in depth analysis of the relationship between microbiota and immune system, since:

1. Advanced Shotgun sequencing is also applied to nasal swabs, in addition to faecal samples. The role of nasal microbiota, and its relationship with gut microbiota, will be explored for the first time in GD and GO patients;
2. Metagenomics data are integrated with metabolomics and proteomics analysis performed on plasma, faecal and nasal samples;
3. Such advanced microbiota's analyses are also integrated with paired immunophenotyping of lymphocytes resident within the organs targeted by autoimmunity in GD and GO patients (thyroid and lymph node) accessed by fine-needle aspiration (FNA), to study the bidirectional modulation between microbiota and immune system.

The final goal of MISS.GO study, thanks to such integrated analysis of fecal and nasal metagenomics, metabolomics and metaproteomics, together with paired tissue-resident immunophenotyping, is to improve the current knowledge of GD and GO pathogenesis, aiming to identify prognostic GD and GO markers, predictive factors for GO development, and key microbiota and immune signatures that can be exploited for prevention, mitigation and therapeutic strategies.

brief_summary: Inspiratory muscle training (IMT) is a relatively simple and accessible form of exercise that specifically targets the respiratory muscles and has been reported to improve inspiratory muscle strength, respiratory efficiency, exercise capacity, and autonomic cardiovascular regulation in different populations. Given the close relationship between respiratory muscle function, exercise capacity, autonomic regulation, and metabolic health, IMT may represent a potentially useful adjunctive intervention for women with PCOS. Therefore, investigating the effects of inspiratory muscle training on relevant metabolic, functional, and clinical outcomes in women with PCOS may provide an additional therapeutic approach within physiotherapy and lifestyle-based management.
primary_outcomes: Homeostatic model assessment of IR (HOMA- IR),
title: Inspiratory Muscle Training for the Management of Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome

brief_summary: This randomised controlled trial will evaluate the effects of integrating a standalone mixed-reality (MR) breathing and eye-gaze training intervention (EyeBreathe) into regular basketball practice for adolescent athletes in Latvia. Participants will be individually randomised to either a six-week MR intervention (two sessions per week) or to continue usual training. Assessments before and after the intervention will measure heart rate and heart rate variability, CO₂ tolerance, breathing pattern, reactive stress tolerance, and pre-competition anxiety. Sessions will be supervised at first, then completed independently via password-protected headset profiles. Intervention adherence will be monitored. The primary efficacy analysis will use a prespecified per-protocol population, defined as intervention participants who complete at least four of the twelve scheduled sessions.
primary_outcomes: Reactive stress tolerance
title: EyeBreathe: A Mixed Reality Game With Eye Tracking and Breathing Biofeedback for Adolescent Basketball Players - A Randomised Controlled Trial

brief_summary: This retrospective single-centre case series evaluates the feasibility and clinical outcomes of selective open Desarda repair for inguinal hernia in adolescent males treated in a paediatric surgical department. The study focuses on recurrence, postoperative complications, reoperation, persistent groin pain, postoperative length of stay, and follow-up after Desarda repair.
primary_outcomes: Number of Desarda repairs with clinically documented ipsilateral inguinal hernia recurrence

brief_summary: Periodontal health is influenced by various local and systemic factors, with smoking being one of the major environmental risk factors. This clinical study is designed to investigate the biochemical profiles of individuals by measuring apelin, periostin, and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP) levels in both gingival crevicular fluid and serum. The participants will be divided into specific study groups based on their smoking status and periodontal condition. Samples of gingival crevicular fluid and serum will be collected under standard clinical protocols, and biomarker concentrations will be analyzed quantitatively using the ELISA (Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay) method to evaluate their potential correlation with periodontal status.
primary_outcomes: Apelin, Periostin, and hs-CRP levels in Gingival Crevicular Fluid (GCF) and Serum
title: Evaluation of the Effect of Smoking on Apelin, Periostin, and High-Sensitivity CRP Levels in Gingival Crevicular Fluid and Serum

brief_summary: This cross-sectional observational study aims to investigate the prevalence and associated factors of neck and shoulder pain in homemakers aged 25-55 years. The study will examine the relationships between neck and shoulder pain and demographic characteristics, duration and type of housework, fatigue, physical activity, smartphone and social media use, hobbies, posture, functional status, instrumental activities of daily living, and health-related quality of life. Neck-related disability will be assessed using the Neck Disability Index, upper extremity function using the Disabilities of the Arm, Shoulder and Hand (DASH) questionnaire, instrumental activities of daily living using the Lawton and Brody Instrumental Activities of Daily Living Scale, quality of life using the SF-12 Health Survey, and posture using the New York Posture Rating Chart. The findings are expected to contribute to identifying factors associated with neck and shoulder pain in homemakers and to inform future preventive and rehabilitative approaches.
primary_outcomes: Prevalence of Neck Pain
Prevalence of Shoulder Pain
title: Neck and Shoulder Pain in Homemakers

brief_summary:
Blood pressure can fall during the start of general anesthesia, particularly in older patients with high blood pressure. This study compared two medicines, oliceridine and sufentanil, to assess their effects on low blood pressure during anesthesia induction in older women with hypertension undergoing gynecological laparoscopic surgery.

This single-center randomized controlled trial enrolled 134 women aged 65 to 80 years at the Affiliated Hospital of Nantong University. Participants were assigned to receive either oliceridine or sufentanil, together with the same other anesthesia induction medicines. Blood pressure and heart rate were measured before induction, one minute after induction, immediately after insertion of the breathing tube, and one and five minutes after insertion.

The main outcome was the proportion of participants who experienced low blood pressure during these measurements. Low blood pressure was defined as a mean arterial pressure below 65 mmHg or a decrease of at least 30% from the value measured before induction. Other assessments included changes and variability in blood pressure, heart rate, and the use of medicines to support blood pressure.
primary_outcomes: Incidence of Hypotension During Anesthesia Induction
title: Oliceridine Versus Sufentanil for Blood Pressure Control During Anesthesia Induction in Older Women With Hypertension Undergoing Gynecological Laparoscopic Surgery

brief_summary:
The goal of this phase II, placebo-controlled intervention study is to investigate whether tocilizumab, an interleukin-6 (IL-6) receptor inhibitor, may have a neuroprotective effect by reducing infarct growth in adults with acute ischemic stroke.

The main question it aims to answer is:

Does treatment with tocilizumab given before or during endovascular therapy (EVT) reduce infarct growth 72 hours after EVT compared with placebo in adults with acute ischemic stroke?

Researchers will compare tocilizumab with placebo to determine whether infarct growth is smaller in participants receiving tocilizumab.

Participants will:

Receive either a single dose of tocilizumab or placebo before or during EVT. Undergo standard endovascular treatment for acute ischemic stroke. Undergo brain MRI approximately 72 hours after EVT to assess infarct growth. Have clinical assessments and other study-related examinations and follow-up according to the study protocol.
primary_outcomes: Infarct growth on brain MRI (mL)
title: Infarct Growth After Intravenous Tocilizumab in Adults With Acute Ischemic Stroke Undergoing Endovascular Thrombectomy - ILLUMINATE
